Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Blackpool, Milton Keynes, Sheffield and Wrexham have made the final shortlist to be named the UK City of Culture for 2029.

According to the Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS), the four candidates will each be given at least £125,000 to develop their proposals for the chance to secure the title alongside a £10 million prize fund.

Bidding locations were asked to outline how cultural initiatives could act as a catalyst to transform their area and enrich community life by fostering growth, opportunities and pride.

The designation is awarded every four years and is presently held by Bradford.

The shortlist was recommended by the UK City of Culture expert advisory panel, which is chaired by Brookside and Hollyoaks creator Sir Phil Redmond.

Sir Phil said: “Once again there is a hard choice ahead.

“The four places on the shortlist continue to demonstrate both the variety and strength of creative ambition across the UK.

open image in gallery The title is awarded every four years and is currently held by Bradford ( The Independent )

“Each place represents a different view, or aspect, epitomising what culture is, the sum of all we do together, and while each approaches it differently, they all share the common aim of reminding the rest of the UK of who they are, where they are and why they are worth visiting.

“I look forward to doing that myself, along with the rest of the Advisory Panel in the near future.”

The competition is part of the Government’s drive to boost pride in every part of the country and encourage economic growth.

According to the DCMS, the cultural spotlight helped attract millions of pounds in additional investment and boosted regeneration among previous winning cities including, Derry-Londonderry, Hull and Coventry.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: “Every place has a story worth telling of its own unique history, identity and contribution.

“Great culture is everywhere, but the opportunity to showcase it, to put it on display and to show how it is woven into our national story is not.

“That is the beauty of the UK City of Culture competition, it is an undiluted celebration of what makes our largest towns and cities so brilliant.”

Last year, Bradford led a cultural programme of over 6,500 events, over 80% of which were free, that resulted in capital investment for more than 30 local cultural organisations.

The DCMS said it also led to increased opportunities for local people to get involved with events, with over 88,000 residents taking part in key projects throughout the year.

Ms Nandy continued: “Congratulations to Blackpool, Milton Keynes, Sheffield and Wrexham on making the shortlist.

“They are proud of their incredible culture, and they are right to be.”

The UK City of Culture 2029 winner will be announced in early 2027.

News.title: Trump boots The Independent from Air Force One after Oval Office meltdown
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump’s communications staff has removed The Independent’s White House correspondent from the traveling press pool that was scheduled to cover his trip to Iowa for a campaign rally on Thursday.

Correspondent Andrew Feinberg was notified by the White House Press Office on Wednesday evening that he will “not be the print pooler on tomorrow’s trip” despite his scheduled shift in the rotation, which was confirmed days earlier.

“Thank you for your understanding,” the sparse message read.

The notice arrived one day after the president berated Feinberg inside the Oval Office, where Trump told him to “be careful” after trying to ask questions he didn’t like. He also labeled him a “sick person,” adding, “I actually think there’s something wrong with you.”

An official White House rapid response account on X also called him a “Mongoloid Moron” while Vice President JD Vance used his official government X account to call him an “imbecile.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump on Wednesday abruptly removed The Independent’s White House reporter off his planned coverage rotation on Air Force One for the trip to an Iowa midterms rally on October 22 ( Getty Images )

The Independent is at least the third outlet to be removed from Air Force One in recent weeks following the president’s growing threats to media access and a high-profile lawsuit seeking a court’s intervention to reverse what the president has called a “ban” on three other outlets.

A federal judge has ordered the administration to restore press passes that belonged to several journalists from CNN, Politico and MS NOW, which the president said he was “banning” from the White House, likely in violation of the First and Fifth Amendments.

But reporters from CNN and Politico continue to be barred from Air Force One on days their outlets have been assigned to provide out-of-town print or television coverage of the president’s travel.

Administration officials have sought to distinguish the removal of individual outlets and reporters from the White House, which a judge has rejected, to pool coverage on Air Force One.

In a recent interview with TIME, Trump denied that he was violating the court’s order. White House communications director Steven Cheung also said restoring press passes is “different than allowing the pool into the events in the Oval Office or on Air Force One.”

The White House previously told The Independent that traveling on Air Force One is a “privilege not a right” and defended Trump as “the most accessible President in American history” who “will continue to grant an unprecedented level of access to the press.”

open image in gallery Within the last month, at least three outlets have been barred from Air Force One on days they are assigned to provide out-of-town print or television coverage ( AFP/Getty )

On Wednesday, before traveling to a campaign rally in South Carolina, the president again lashed out at members of the press who asked him questions outside the White House

He called CNN’s Kaitlain Collins a “low IQ person” and a “dummy” and called a reporter for ABC News a “stupid person.”

“You don’t know what you’re talking about,” he told Collins as he waved her off. “You're a low-IQ person, you're a dummy, and you work for CNN.”

Last week, Trump-appointed District Judge Timothy Kelly determined that the president likely violated the law by revoking press passes for CNN, MSNOW and Politico journalists. Less than 24 hours later, the administration appealed the order, launching a legal battle that will likely play out in courts for months while reporters fight for access to the president.

The Department of Justice has argued that the outlets were banned for national security reasons, though the president has not made any such argument. The White House Press Office only raised those concerns in letters to the outlets after a lawsuit was filed to reverse the ban.

In his order, Judge Kelly wrote that the president’s public statements justifying the “ban” clearly show that he targeted the outlets for their coverage, not national security concerns.

“Simply put, that is unlawful viewpoint discrimination,” he wrote.

Trump is scheduled to appear at a campaign rally in Sioux City, Iowa on Thursday to support U.S. Senate candidate Ashley Hinson, gubernatorial candidate Zach Lahn and other Republicans on the ballot.

News.title: Teacher who survived Oregon school attack says she had no chance to protect children
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A teacher wounded in last week's attack on a special education classroom at an Oregon elementary school says she never had a chance to try to shelter any of the children inside.

In a statement issued by a family friend, Becky Drury said Wednesday that she ran to see what was going on when she realized something was happening — but immediately saw the shooter and rushed back to the classroom.

“I turned to shut the door behind me, but the shooter was already there,” Drury said. “Before I could do anything more, he shot me at close range and I fell to the ground.”

Her left hand was nearly severed by a gunshot, and her right arm was struck as well. Unable to get up or defend herself or others, she said, “I did the only thing I could do, which was to pretend to be dead in the hope he would not shoot me again.”

Three children — ages 5, 8 and 11 — and a teacher were killed at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, last Thursday when a former student there, 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, blasted his way through locked doors with a shotgun and attacked the classroom. Another student was critically injured.

Authorities said another teacher threw her phone at the gunman and then tackled him and wrestled with him for control of the weapon, likely saving lives before the gunman was shot by a father who followed him into the building.

Some news reports had suggested that Drury threw herself on top of one student to protect her. Drury, who remains hospitalized, said she wanted to correct the record.

“Accurate, respectful reporting is a truly important service that will help heal the wounds inflicted by that awful day,” she said.

School reopened in the district Wednesday for the first time since the shooting. Dozens of officers were on hand at each school to welcome children back, the Bend Police Department said.

In a social media post, the department said it continues investigating the attack, including serving search warrants at the attacker's home, as well as on his electronic devices and his social media accounts on a variety of platforms.

The statement said police have confirmed that the pump-action shotgun used in the attack had been legally purchased. The Associated Press previously reported it had been purchased by the suspect's mother, according to a law enforcement source who was not authorized to discuss the investigation. But investigators said they were still looking into how the boy obtained it.

News.title: Harry Kane proves there can only be one Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants
News.content:
In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

News.title: Carrick apology to United fans ominously similar to Solskjaer’s final match
News.content:
There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

News.title: Ebola case confirmed in Nigeria as outbreak spreads through Africa
News.content:
African ministers have been called to an urgent health summit after Nigeria confirmed its first case in the outbreak of the deadly Ebola fever tearing through eastern Congo.

Confirmation of a case in Africa’s most populous nation came days after a cluster was detected in Kenya and has heightened questions about border screening checks designed to stop the virus spreading from its epicentre in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

With cases now found in West Africa, Central Africa and East Africa, the epidemic “has already become the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history,” said Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the continent’s main public health body.

DRC has recorded close to 10,000 cases since an outbreak began in mid-May, with around half of them dying of the haemorrhagic fever.

The Nigeria case meant “Ebola is now affecting three regions of Africa,” warned Dr Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

“The situation demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level,” he said, convening an online summit for next week.

News.title: One billion children at risk from heatwaves, WHO warns
News.content:
More than one billion children are exposed to increasingly severe heat waves, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

1.5 billion children under one experienced a fivefold increase in the number of heat wave days in 2024 compared with the 1986 to 2005 baseline period, jumping from roughly four days per year to a high of over 20, says the health agency. And these periods of high temperature are becoming longer, more frequent and more severe, the WHO warns.

According to the Met Office, this summer was the hottest on record in the UK, with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days where the temperature was above 30 degrees celsius. Europe also saw record-breaking temperatures, and Asia and Africa both experienced their warmest July on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

Four UN agencies, including the WHO, the WMO, Unicef and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), have urged countries to monitor how extreme heat affects pregnant women, newborns and children.

The new framework tracks preterm birth, stillbirths, low birthweight, pregnancy hypertension, child deaths and health facility visits.

“Heat is already affecting our most vulnerable populations, including pregnant women, newborns and children. But what health systems do not count, they cannot respond to,” said Dr Pascale Allotey, director of WHO’s department of maternal and child health.

“By tracking outcomes such as preterm birth, child deaths and illnesses, and health-facility visits alongside heat exposure, countries can identify potential impacts and take action to protect women and children,” she said.

High temperatures are particularly dangerous for pregnant women because the body has to work much harder to cool both the mother and the baby.

Intense heat can cause surface-level blood vessels to dilate, which in pregnant women can restrict blood flow to the placenta and reduce the amount of oxygen and nutrients that reach the foetus. Heat can also put strain on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, dangerously high blood pressure, and pre-eclampsia.

The odds of a preterm birth also increase by 26 per cent during heatwaves: for every one degree rise in heat exposure, the likelihood of giving birth early rise by roughly 4 per cent, according to a systematic review published in Nature Medicine.

The WHO has also urged countries to develop and implement tailored heat-health action plans that account for the needs of pregnant women, newborns and children, as well as strengthening early-warning systems to ensure timely action to heat risks, such as alert systems and personalised public messaging.

“As our world continues to heat up, it creates new risks for health, and older people, pregnant women, newborns and children are among those least able to escape them,” said Bruce Gordon, director of environment and climate change at the WHO.

“Our health systems need the data to recognise this reality and take action – from protecting people during heatwaves to embedding climate risk consideration into everyday health services,” he said.

News.title: Rio Ngumoha dazzles on coming-of-age night in Europe
News.content:
Iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

“They are so good on the ball,” Iraola said of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

“We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he said, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

Virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker, who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas, who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

News.title: Inflation jumps in run-up to Healey’s maiden Budget
News.content:
Inflation has jumped to its highest level in almost a year, underlining the challenges facing John Healey, the Chancellor, ahead of his first Budget next week.

The consumer prices index climbed from 3.1pc in August to 3.5pc in September, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

Inflation was ahead of the 3.4pc predicted by economists and is now at its highest level since October 2025.

The sharp rise was driven by soaring fuel costs as a result of the Iran war. The ONS said average petrol prices rose by 8.2p a litre in September and diesel by 10.7p. Both reached levels not seen since 2022, in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales, said: “Rising inflation is turning the Budget into a perilous high-wire act for the Chancellor, increasing pressure for cost-of-living support while pushing up government borrowing costs, which is shrinking fiscal headroom and narrowing his policy options.”

Britain spent more money on debt interest last month than in any September on record, official figures show.

The UK’s debt servicing costs rose to £10.9bn in September, the highest total for the month since at least 1997, according to the ONS.

This burden helped to push national debt above £3 trillion for the first time.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said the unhappy milestone and the rise in inflation “show Labour has lost control of the economy”.

Public sector net debt has soared by 50pc since it first exceeded £2tn in June 2020.

Mr Healey insisted the British economy still had “momentum” and pointed to Wednesday morning’s approval of new drilling for gas in the North Sea as evidence of this.

He said: “We know that price rises from conflicts in the Middle East and Europe are hitting Britain and countries worldwide. Last week, the IMF said our UK fiscal discipline stands out with the lowest forecast deficit in the G7 by 2029.

“And today we’ve given the green light to getting North Sea gas from the Jackdaw field, investing the revenues in our clean energy future and supporting British workers.

“In my Budget next week, I will keep up this momentum. Maintaining our fiscal discipline and drive for growth in every postcode, while giving businesses and families some breathing space.”

September’s inflation figure is used for the annual uprating of welfare payments, with the state pension now in line to rise by almost £500 next year.

The figure is also used to calculate increases in business rates in England, with pubs, shops, offices and other hospitality businesses now facing a £1.1bn increase in the collective bill from April, according to tax firm Ryan.

News.title: England dealt harsh lesson in Pakistan collapse
News.content:
Brendon McCullum wants his team to learn how to adapt as they prepare for the World Cup and this was a lesson in how not to master a run chase.

Failing to overhaul 302 is not an embarrassment, but the way England threw away a good start with some brittle batting gives McCullum plenty to ponder.

Spin exposed familiar failings as left-armer Arafat Minhas added six for 40 to his 59 from 58 with the bat, but it was also short balls from the seamers that hurt England. A two-paced pitch made the back-of-a-length delivery tricky, as it had in the match between Sri Lanka and Pakistan on the same ground at the weekend, but England failed to find a way to adjust their tempo.

Ben Duckett, Joe Root and Sam Curran were all dismissed by seamers hitting the pitch hard and forcing them to play square while Arafat exposed limitations against spin. He bowled Harry Brook for five with a beauty that dipped and straightened as he mixed up his arm ball with consistent accuracy to deadly effect.

Sports.title: Odds SLASHED on Michael Carrick to be next Premier League manager sacked after Man Utd horror show at Como
Sports.content:
Next

THE odds on Michael Carrick to be sacked as Manchester United manager have been SLASHED following the Red Devils’ European disaster.

United made it consecutive Champions League losses as they got smashed by competition debutants Como, managed by Cesc Fabregas, on Wednesday evening.



Betfair have seen Carrick to be sacked next markets slashed from 2-1 into a short 17-20.

Betfair spokesperson James Mackie said: “Michael Carrick’s tenure as Manchester United manager took another bleak turn on Wednesday evening as his side lost 4-1 away to Italian side Como in the Champions League.



“The Red Devils are now winless in their last seven matches and after tonight’s slaughtering in Italy, Carrick has been slashed into 17/20 from 2/1 to be the next manager to leave the Premier League.

“Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe has emerged as the 9-4 favourite to take over at Old Trafford if Michael Carrick was to be let go from his job, with Antonio Conte and Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler both joint second-favourites at 5/1.

“Other names emerging as possible options to take the Manchester United job are Cesc Fabregas at 11/1 who was the man in charge of United’s 4-1 battering on Wednesday night, and England boss Thomas Tuchel is a 14/1 chance.

“How long can Michael Carrick last as Manchester United manager…”

The Geordie former midfielder slammed his own players and personally apologised to the travelling fans following the disastrous loss in Como.

Fabregas was asked about the job at United in his pre-match press conference, but quickly batted it off as disrespectful.

Fabregas said: “I won’t answer that question because I think that’s not a very nice question.

“I don’t think that shows enough respect to a great footballer and manager like Michael Carrick at the helm of a wonderful Manchester United side.”

Sports.title: Tottenham flop Tanguy Ndombele, 29, on TRIAL at European minnows as he looks to revive career
Sports.content:
Next

TOTTENHAM flop Tanguy Ndombele is on TRIAL at Russian club Rubin Kazan.

The French midfielder, once Spurs’ record signing when he arrived from Lyon for £63million in 2019, has been a free agent since leaving Nice in the summer.



But Kazan, currently 11th in the Russian Premier League, have given his fading career a lifeline.

On Instagram the club said: “He will be at our club for observation and will spend a training cycle with the team, after which a decision about his future will be made.”



Ndombele was once one of Europe’s most highly-rated midfielders when he joined Tottenham but he never lived up to expectations despite the odd flash of brilliance.

And his last outing for the club – an FA Cup tie against Morecambe in 2022 – summed up his time after being loudly booed by his own fans for showing no urgency to leave the pitch when he was substituted.

He only played 91 times for the North Londoners, scoring ten times, before being shipped out on consecutive loans to Lyon, Napoli and Galatasaray.

In 2024, Spurs decided to settle on a figure to pay up the final year of his £200,000-a-week deal.

Ndombele, 29, returned to France with Nice, but played just 38 games across two seasons and was restricted to just 13 outings last term.

Sports.title: Aston Villa 3 Viking 1: Unai Emery’s side maintain perfect Champions League start by brushing aside Norwegians
Sports.content:
Next

ASTON VILLA are one of the best teams in Europe… For now at least.

Unai Emery‘s side rose to second in the Champions League league phase with a comfortable 3-1 win over Norweigan side Viking at Villa Park, which made it three wins from three.



First-half goals from Ross Barkley and Emiliano Buendia had them level with PSG and Liverpool on nine points, with an own goal from Henrik Heggheim taking them to second on goal difference, even without the likes of new boy Johan Manzambi.

Under Emery, there will be Villa fans dreaming of a deep run in Europe this season, with a few seriously optimistic ones thinking they could even win it – if their pre-match tifo was anything to go by.



The Holte End unveiled a huge banner with a picture of the Villa Villain that read: “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more.”

And if anyone knows how to thrive in European competitions, after all, it’s Spanish boss Emery who won them the Europa League last season, with only Jose Mourinho and Carlo Ancelotti matching his five European titles.



If his side could play every match at Villa Park they might even be favourites, with the victory taking them to ELEVEN straight home wins in Europe – only Manchester United and Manchester City have won more than ten in a row this century.

The first half had Villa in second place, only behind PSG atop the table.

But truth be told, they should have been top after 26 minutes.

Nicolas Jackson had two headers saved by Arild Østbø in the opening ten minutes before Barkley did what he couldn’t and wheeled off in celebration after nodding home from an Ibrahim Mbaye corner 12 minutes later.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The biggest miss of the night, and potentially of the season for Villa, came just moments later.

An Alysson cross was palmed into the onrushing Buendia, who missed from six yards out despite being completely unmarked – and to make matters worse, the Argentine forward missed again before half an hour had been played.

Eventually, he got his goal.

It was a case of trip by name, trip by nature as Zlatko Tripic stuck a leg out to bring down Alysson in the penalty area, which was waved away by the referee only to be given by VAR.

Buendia made no mistake from the spot, rolling the ball into the bottom right corner to double Villa’s lead before half-time.



Some might say “It’s only Viking…” and that a clean sheet should be expected against this level of opposition.

But those people would be forgetting that the Eliteserien champions drew 3-3 with Bayern Munich just a week ago.

Any attempts of scoring three at Villa Park, though, were claimed by Zion Suzuki, who is proving a stellar signing between the sticks.



Viking ventured forward more often in search of a second half comeback, but it left them open to Villa’s electrifying attack on the break with Alysson forcing a Heggheim own goal with half an hour still to play.

In that half-hour it only really looked like Villa would add more goals rather than concede any, with Jackson missing the target once more before being swapped for Tammy Abraham up front as Emery made a host of changes.

That brought on the inevitable chants of “We are top of the league.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But they dropped back down to second following an 84th-minute consolation strike from Peter Christiansen.

Villa’s next Champions League game is a visit to Barcelona in two weeks’ time, before a tough trip to Galatasaray and a real test of that impeccable home record against PSG before Christmas.

Rice then popped up with a low, drilled finish eight minutes from the end of normal time as Arsenal picked up a good point, which was tarnished only by Bukayo Saka hobbling off early on.

The result extends the North Londoners’ league phase unbeaten run to a whopping 15 matches.



SunSport’s Arsenal correspondent Simon Collings goes through three key talking points from the Allianz Arena.

That’s the spirit!

It was a brilliant game of football and a really good result for Arsenal given the circumstances.

We talk a lot about Arsenal’s style, don’t we? And maybe you can question that, but you cannot question their spirit.

What a brilliant performance. They showed so much heart, so much hunger at the Allianz Arena.

When you go behind and it’s your chief tormentor, Harry Kane, you could easily lose heart.

But Arsenal didn’t and they deserve a lot of credit for that.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Eze does it

Eberechi Eze summed up Arsenal’s heart and fight tonight.

He had a really difficult game at Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

He was hooked at half-time and could not get into the match.

Here, he comes off the bench, scores a goal and looks absolutely fantastic.

Eze was really, really impressive, and that could be a big thing given Bukayo Saka’s injury.



Sak’d off

I’ve got to admit, he did not look very good.

Sports.title: I’ll have my ‘four in a row’ leg tattoo removed if Man City are stripped of their Prem titles, reveals Kyle Walker
Sports.content:
Next

FORMER Man City skipper Kyle Walker says he will have his “4 in a row” leg tattoo removed if the club are stripped of their Premier League titles.

Walker, 36, is the first Blues star to publicly address the scandal after City were found guilty of more than 100 financial breaches, although they are appealing against the decision.



He said of losing his inking celebrating the team’s streak of Prem trophies: “I’m probably going to have to do that.”

Right-back Walker, now with Burnley in the Championship, said: “Let’s not hide from the fact that, you know, they’ve been found guilty, but they’re going through an appeal.



“Now, as a player, all I can say is that all we did is go out and play our best football as a team and I will defend the players for the rest of my life.

“I feel that what we did and what we achieved in that space of time was probably incredible and probably won’t be done ever again.



“But from the outside looking in, it doesn’t look great and we have to address that.”

City could face expulsion from the Premier League for inflating revenue by more than £900million through illicit state-backed sponsorships.



Although the verdicts relate to 2009 to 2018, possible sanctions could cover the “four in a row” league title streak from 2020 to 2024.

Walker, co-hosting talkSPORT Drive! with Andy Goldstein, said he hoped he would avoid having to have his tattoo removed.

He added: “There’s only a select few of us that can say that we won four . . . I’ll try and keep it on, but hopefully we don’t get the things taken away.”

In more trouble for the club, a Freedom of Information request shows City’s Abu Dhabi owners bagged a £10million-a-year naming rights package for the team’s ground from state-funded Etihad Airways.



Yet under a deal with Manchester City Council, local taxpayers got no more than £750,000 a year.

The stadium was built for the 2002 Commonwealth Games using £112million of taxpayer and lottery cash and was leased by the council to City.

Professor Jon Silver, of Sheffield University’s Urban Institute, said that as the land and facilities remain a public asset used by a private enterprise, “further scrutiny is required”.

The council said income from its freehold deal with the club — including rental income, naming rights and potential uplift via European fixtures — was ring-fenced for sport and leisure investment in Manchester.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 2: Declan Rice scores late equaliser after Harry Kane magic but Bukayo Saka limps off injured
Sports.content:
Next

FORGET about a week being a long time in football, try four days.

Eberechi Eze was on the floor on Sunday, hooked at half time following a woeful performance in a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.



But he picked himself up off the floor to inspire Arsenal to an impressive draw here at Bayern Munich.

Eze scored Arsenal’s opening goal and summed up their fighting spirit during a performance where they showed so much heart.



This side just do not know when they are beaten, as shown by Noni Madueke’s late winner at Forest.

Eze’s opener in the 25th minute, here, was cancelled out by Alphonso Davies before the break and a Harry Kane penalty just after the hour mark.

But Arsenal roared back late on, claiming a point thanks to Declan Rice and extending their unbeaten league phase run in the Champions League to 15 games.

It was so fitting for Eze to be at the heart of it and he only got his chance to shine after Bukayo Saka limped off injured.

The winger injured his left quad in the first 10 minutes and then forced Eze to come on.

The England star put himself about and ensured this was not another miserable Munich night for Arsenal.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

They have had plenty in Bavaria, losing their last three trips – and two of those were 5-1 hammerings.

This was the perfect response to ending that poor record and should give Arsenal confidence going forward.

They reached the final of the Champions League last season and look like contenders to go deep once more.

The omens were not good for Arsenal coming into this game.

The Gunners may have beaten Bayern Munich at home last season, but the German champions are a different beast at the Allianz Arena.



Bayern were also looking to extend a 39-game unbeaten run at home in Champions League group and league phase matches, dating back to 2013.

Arsenal’s spirits may have been lifted, however, when they saw the hosts’ team.

Star winger Michael Olise was missing due to suspension and Luis Diaz was absent from the other flank after being named on the bench.

There was also no Joshua Kimmich – left out entirely following the death of his father.



But goalkeeper Manuel Neuer had recovered from a foot problem to start and, of course, Kane was there to lead the line.

Head coach Vincent Kompany, who had got over a virus to be in the dugout, has leaned heavily on Kane for his goals.

You wondered if he would be isolated on this occasion, though, without Diaz and Olise flanking him.

The dropping of Diaz from Kompany felt like a nod to the last time Arsenal came here in April 2024, when they lost 1-0 to crash out at the quarter-final stage.



Thomas Tuchel, who was head coach at the time, played two left-backs on that occasion to shut down Saka.

Kompany had seemingly copied that by starting Davies in tandem with Josip Stanisic.

But Saka’s night was over after 10 minutes as he limped off having appeared to injure his left thigh.

It forced Mikel Arteta into an early reshuffle.

Madueke, who had come into the team on the left flank, moved to the right and Eze replaced Saka.



The change could have knocked Arsenal off their stride after a brisk start, but they continued to impress.

Martin Odegaard was at the heart of it, pulling the strings in midfield, and it was no surprise he created the opening goal.

The offside flag went up, yet VAR intervened to give Eze a moment he would have savoured.



Arsenal were deservedly ahead and it took an equally excellent assist to peg them back.

Kane – who else – played a perfect pass through to Davies and he did not have to break stride as he levelled 10 minutes after Eze’s opener.

Bayern and Kane’s tails were up after that.

The England captain had been like an NFL quarter-back in the opening 30 minutes, even taking a goal kick to create one chance for Serge Gnabry.

Both sides could have gone ahead right at the start of the second half.

Sports.title: Alysson stars as Villa beat Viking to make it three wins from three in Europe
Sports.content:
Aston Villa made it three wins from three in the Champions League with a 3-1 win over Viking at Villa Park.

Ross Barkley headed Unai Emery's side in front midway through the first half and Emiliano Buendia's penalty made it two before the break. Alysson's run led to an own goal for the third with only Peter Christiansen's late volley taking Villa off top spot.

Bayern Munich struggled against the Norwegian champions last week but Villa were in control from the start despite a makeshift look to the side with Joao Gomes at right-back. The Brazilian had a cross deflected against the underside of the bar early in the game.

Image: Ross Barkley celebrates scoring Aston Villa's opening goal against Viking

Ibrahim Mbaye's corner from the other flank was nodded in by Barkley soon after before Buendia came close with two good headed chances. The Argentine made amends from the penalty spot when a VAR check ruled that Alysson had been clipped inside the box.

The young winger was the best player on the pitch, producing surely his best performance in a Villa shirt. He was instrumental in the third goal too, racing through from deep. Henrik Heggheim could only divert his cross past his own goalkeeper.

That was the goal that took Villa into top spot in this league phase. The crowd knew it too, chanting 'We are top of the league' afterwards. But Peter Christiansen's brilliant late volley - awarded after a VAR check - dropped them back to second behind PSG.

The tifo unveiled in the Holte End before kick-off pointed out that Villa have conquered before and are prepared for more. There are more fancied sides in this Champions League but few boast the clarity of purpose that Emery brings. Villa are building again.

Aston Villa's win in stats

Aston Villa are the second quickest team to record 20 wins in the European Cup (30 matches), behind only Real Madrid (29 matches).

Villa have won each of their last 12 major European home games, the joint-longest run by an English team this century.

Villa are the first Europa League holders to win their first three games of a Champions League campaign since Manchester United in 2017.

Buendia: Alysson was incredible

Emiliano Buendia speaking about Alysson to TNT Sports:

"He was incredible. He's showing his potential, his ability on the wing. Also Ibrahim Mbaye as well - their speed, their qualities. It's going to help the team a lot, so it's very important to have them and to try to help them to improve because they are young talents."

Emery: Some players did a step forward

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking in the press conference:

"We are delighted how we are responding in our demands, respecting the competition of the Champions League and respecting the opponent, and how we are improving things. Through those issues I think we played a good match, collectively, tactically, respecting them, following the plan we set on.

"Then, individually, the players showed their qualities. I think we did a good job and some players did a step forward in their confidence, feeling better, understanding everything tactically and playing their football."

Emery likely had his wingers in mind. When asked about Mbaye and Alysson, he replied: "It was a step forward for both players in our idea, so really happy." There was praise too for Alejandro Garnacho who "played his best minutes" in a late cameo off the bench.

Viking boss: They were all over us

Viking head coach Morten Jensen speaking in the press conference:

"The second half was much more like Viking wants to be. Maybe we had too much respect in the first half, they were all over us and we did not create much offensively, which is rare for Viking.

"I think we did a much better job by asking questions of Villa's midfield and their defence and ended up drawing the second half. That is something that we can build on for the future.

"It is the next level for us as a team and really great to see the team get a goal at Villa Park in front of over 2,000 Norwegian fans."

Image: Emi Buendia doubled Aston Villa's lead over Viking from the penalty spot

37 - GOAL! Buendia made it two from the penalty spot

62 - OWN GOAL! Heggheim turned in Alysson's cross

84 - GOAL! Christiansen's volley brings consolation

Sports.title: Fernandes criticises coaches, Carrick criticises players - but who was to blame?
Sports.content:
Who was to blame for Manchester United's miserable 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League?

Bruno Fernandes criticised the tactical plan of the Man Utd coaches.

Michael Carrick questioned the motivation of his players.

If only Man Utd's performance on the pitch in Italy was as forceful as the post-match interviews.

After losing at Atletico Madrid last time out in the Champions League, Lisandro Martinez hit out at the club's hierarchy, calling out technical director Jason Wilcox for failings in the transfer window.

This time captain Fernandes took aim at the club's coaching staff in a stinging take-down of their pressing plan.

Image: Bruno Fernandes during Man Utd's defeat to Como

Asked by TNT Sports about a lack of cohesion in United's work out of possession, Fernandes defended his team-mates and put the blame on Carrick and his coaches.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," he said.

Free pass? Como rack up big numbers vs Man Utd Como completed 594 passes, the most by a team in a Champions League game against Manchester United since Barcelona in April 2019 (725).

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

Was that tactical idea what cost Man Utd in Como? "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me," said Fernandes.

A meeting between Carrick, Martinez and Wilcox repaired relations after the centre-back's comments in Madrid. But Carrick gave a blunt response in his post-match press conference on Wednesday when Fernandes' thoughts were put to him.

For all United did wrong in the game, it was the application of his players which was prominent in his post-match assessment.

"I'll definitely look at what we've done [as a coaching staff] or if it's the motivation and the intention and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football you have to bring," he said. "We didn't bring that today.

"You can't turn it on and off and you can't choose when you want to perform or when you don't want to perform or when you give absolutely everything or when you maybe don't," he told TNT Sports.

Sports.title: Miserable Man Utd ripped apart by Como
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's Manchester United were ripped apart in a dreadful 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League, as their miserable run of results stretched to seven without a win.

The pressure continues to pile on Carrick and this United side as their start to the season lurches from bad to worse - and on Wednesday night they were humbled by a Como team that delivered more intensity and quality in Italy.

The first attribute should be a non-negotiable but, despite United's application being in the spotlight, they were once again outworked by their opposition. Static in midfield, allowing Como players to run off them, losing markers... this was a shocking show of United's big failings out of possession.

The tone was set just two minutes in when Man Utd went behind early on - again. They are the first English side to concede in back-to-back Champions League games so soon and never got to grips with Cesc Fabregas' impressively coached team.

Nico Paz brought the class for the hosts. The talented Argentina international stuck the opener into the top corner when Harry Maguire gave him too much space and then slotted in a third after catching Carlos Baleba in possession.

Paz set up another Como goal, too, playing in Tasos Douvikas, who ran away from a disoriented Matthijs de Ligt to find the net inside four minutes of the second half.

Image: Diogo Dalot during Man Utd's Champions League match with Como

This was De Ligt's first start in 325 days due to back problems and came due to a wider spate of injuries at the club. But excuses for this United performance may wear thin quickly for the travelling support who stood in the pouring rain to watch this dismantling.

United's own star, Bruno Fernandes, was anonymous again, with just one goal involvement now in his past nine appearances for the club. His head-shaking summed up the mood before a sweeping Como fourth, which saw unmarked centre-back Jacobo Ramon head in, underlining the vast gap between the sides on the night.

Joshua Zirkzee's injury-time goal was of little consolation. With just three points from their first three games, United have an uphill battle to make it out of the league phase in this competition. More immediately they are in desperate need of a better performance and win at home to Bournemouth on Sunday in the Premier League, live on Sky Sports.

Carrick 'really angry' with Man Utd performance

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United boss Michael Carrick admits their performance was 'not acceptable' in their 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick:

"I'm really angry but you've got to move on and deal with what's next. At this moment in time, there's a lot to do before the next game to get the team ready, because that was a difficult night for everybody.

"It's not about playing for me - it's about playing for this club. My whole life's wrapped around it [Man Utd]. I genuinely give everything I possibly can. It's not about me, it's about what we all give."

Asked if all of the players give as much as he does, Carrick said: "I'd like to think so. I didn't like what I saw tonight though."

Analysis: No shock to see Man Utd beaten

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson criticised Manchester United after they were thrashed 4-1 in the Champions League by Como

Sky Sports' Paul Merson:

"They've got to start winning matches. The problem with Manchester United is we still live in the age of when it was [Wayne] Rooney, [Cristiano] Ronaldo and people like that.

"We're caught by the name - one of the biggest clubs in the world. But they're not one of the biggest teams in the world. They're far from it. Everybody judges them on when they had superstars.

"I don't see it as a shock. I look at their players and I don't go, 'oh this is a surprise'. I didn't expect them to beat Leeds. Absolutely not. I didn't expect them to beat Como. That's where they are.

"Rooney, Ronaldo, [Roy] Keane... they're a million miles away."

'Como defeat is one of Man Utd's worst ever in Europe'

'One of Man Utd's worst ever defeats in Europe'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan provides insight on three things we learned from Manchester United's embarrassing Champions League loss at Como

Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan in Como:

"Michael Carrick looked very angry. He's the first one to defend his players whenever he can.

"It was one of those games where you know from the first minutes that United weren't at it. The body language from some of those players... you could tell Carrick was frustrated.

"Let's not sugar coat it - this is one of their worst ever results in Europe.

"This was a pretty surprising and shocking performance, but I think it's been coming as well. My feeling is that watching this game has told us what we've been thinking about this Manchester United team.

"There will be speculation about how that changing room is feeling and whether Michael Carrick still has them on board. But tonight, it doesn't quite feel everyone is on board.

"Ultimately there's a lot more pressure on Carrick and his position at Manchester United."

Alarming stats for Man Utd

Manchester United are winless in seven consecutive games in all competitions (D3 L4) for the first time since a run of eight matches between November and December 2015.

Manchester United are the first English team to concede inside the opening two minutes of back-to-back major European games (47 seconds vs Atletico Madrid, 118 seconds vs Como).

Como completed 594 passes tonight, the most by a team in a Champions League game against Manchester United since Barcelona in April 2019 (725).

Key moments from Como...

2: BIG MISS! Diogo Dalot takes a Matheus Cunha cross down in the box but his left-foot shot flashes wide of the far post.

2: GOAL! Nico Paz curls Como's opener into the top corner after Harry Maguire gives him too much space. A similar chance to Dalot's - a different result!

17: WIDE! Harry Maguire heads wide from a Bryan Mbeumo cross.

39: BIG MISS! Tasos Douvikas blazes over after stepping into the United box, failing to capitalise on static defending.

41: OFFIDE! A let-off for Senne Lammens and Man Utd as an offside flag goes up against Douvikas after he is brought down in the box by the goalkeeper.

HT: SUBS! Michael Carrick makes two changes at the break with Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba sent on for Andrey Santos and Matheus Cunha.

Image: Como players celebrate taking an early lead against Man Utd in the Champions League

49: GOAL! Man Utd concede at the start of the second half, too, as Paz plays in Douvikas, who runs off Matthijs de Ligt before firing in.

54: CLOSE! Lucas da Cunha blasts a left-foot shot wide from inside the box when he looked primed to add a third.

57: GOAL! Baleba makes an ill-advised turn in his own half with no cover behind him and Paz takes the ball and races in on goal to add a third.

64: CHANCES! But Amad can't connect with Fernandes' clipped pass into the box to pull one back for United. Moments later he sees a shot tipped over.

76: GOAL! Centre-back Jacobo Ramon heads in to finish off another sweeping Como move.

90+1: GOAL! Joshua Zirkzee is narrowly onside to grab a late goal for Man Utd, finding the net after controlling Amad's cross.

Man Utd's next fixtures...

Sports.title: Brilliant sprinter Almeraq retired to stud
Sports.content:
Champion sprinter-elect Almeraq has been retired to stand at Shadwell's Beech House Stud for 2027.

Winner of three six-furlong Group Ones this season for William Haggas and Tom Marquand, that would be a a remarkable season in any book before even considering what happened to him at the end of the 2025 season.

Running in a Listed race at York in September he clipped heels and took a very heavy fall. Connections feared the worst yet while the horses emerged generally unscathed, neither jockey involved, the now-retired Jim Crowley or Trevor Whelan, have ridden since.

For Almeraq to bounce back this season to not only win races but at the very highest level, shows another side to his character.

The four-year-old by Dark Angel won the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot, the Haydock Sprint Cup by over four lengths and on Saturday he took the British Champions Sprint.

Haggas said: "Almeraq has been a fantastic horse and we have always held him in high regard. He is a strong, powerful sprinter with an iron constitution.

"He has done remarkably well to come back from a horrendous fall at York and win three six-furlong Group One races this season, which speaks volumes not only for his ability but also for his mental strength and resilience.

"Combining exceptional speed with versatility, soundness and a lovely temperament, Almeraq has all the attributes to make a very exciting, successful stallion. Everyone at Somerville Lodge wishes him well."

Racing manager Angus Gold told www.shadwellstud.com: "All of us at Shadwell would like to pay tribute to William Haggas and his fantastic team for the incredible job they did in bringing Almeraq back from what could easily have been a career-ending injury at York last year, and turning him into the outstanding sprinter of 2026.

"On top of his natural class, he showed how versatile he was by beating the world's best sprinters on fast ground at Royal Ascot in the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes, easily winning the Betfair Sprint Cup at Haydock on soft ground and then once again showcasing his toughness by running down Paborus on good ground in the Qatar British Champions Sprint at Ascot last weekend.

"His remarkable toughness and consistency, together with his outstanding looks, will make him a very attractive proposition to breeders and we are thrilled to add him to the Beech House Stud team."

Sports.title: England 'not thinking about points difference' against France
Sports.content:
England suffered Rugby League World Cup opening game loss to Tonga; they now have to get a large win against France and then beat Papua New Guinea handsomely to keep slim hopes of progressing to the semi-finals alive; England play France on Saturday October 24 at 7.35am

England's Brad O'Neill says the side will resist the urge to 'go for broke' against France

England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday.

An opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga has left their hopes of reaching the semi-finals hanging by a thread, with points difference looking increasingly like the only way to progress.

But head coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man matchday squad, a sign that he does not plan radical changes against a France team smarting from their 78-4 humbling by Samoa.

O'Neill, the newly-crowned Super League Man of Steel, said: "We have discussed what is required but I feel like the mentality can't be any different to what we had against Tonga.
