Sports.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
Sports.content:
Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra.

I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri.

As a player and a columnist, I never had an issue with Manchester City – precisely because, for many years, the club avoided buying the most obvious superstars. Guardiola said it himself: the most valuable of the valuable do not go to a club such as City, who aren’t even the biggest football brand in their own home town.

Many became world stars in Manchester. Kevin De Bruyne had been discarded by Chelsea, Rodri’s true class was overlooked in Madrid for a long time, Gündogan’s career was on the brink after injuries, and most recently Gianluigi Donnarumma was no longer wanted in Paris. In Germany, City signed players from Hamburg, Frankfurt and Wolfsburg. Erling Haaland in 2022 was the first player they targeted who was also pursued by Bayern Munich. City did not operate like Paris Saint‑Germain did in the era before Luis Enrique.

From the outside, City fundamentally did not do much differently from the other 10 or so top European clubs. But what are achievements on the pitch worth if they are accompanied by rule-breaking? The club have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations between 2009 and 2018. It allegedly invested almost €1bn more than allowed and declared. The league leaders face potential forced relegation or titles being stripped. City continue to deny wrongdoing and are appealing against the decision.

It is right for the Premier League to crack down on unfair competition. I also appreciate that Germany is holding on to the 50+1 rule, which the federal cartel office recently upheld. It ensures that the majority of voting rights must remain with the parent club – the non‑profit section of a professional club. The exceptions that have applied to Leverkusen and Wolfsburg are under review.

View image in fullscreen A Manchester City fan holds up a banner during the club’s Premier League match with Ipswich at the Etihad Stadium. Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images

The bedrock of our football culture is 50+1. This rule exists only in Germany, yet it speaks to a spirit that fits perfectly with the European sports model: 50+1 maintains a balance; on the one hand it allows for investment, on the other it guarantees participation. It strengthens the rights of members and fans. Perhaps it is because of this rule that the average attendance in Germany is higher than anywhere else in the world.

What is the ultimate purpose of football? It is a business, but its infrastructure is still developed by the general public. That is how I have always understood sport. Even as a professional, it was clear to me that my privileged life was made possible by many people working on a voluntary basis. Through my role as tournament director of the European Championship, these political connections have become even clearer to me.

The stadium and football clubs can remain the final places where people gather and society debates its issues only if the elite and the grassroots stay connected, and the public is involved in the process. Football must not be detached from its roots, as was the case with Manchester City. This becomes possible when rules are enforced by an institution. Ideally, not by a commercial entity but by a non-profit one such as Uefa.

In business, as in politics, I am observing a shift in mindset. Today, it is deemed necessary to invest in non‑profit institutions. More and more companies realise that football allows for a genuine exchange with the population – that it provides the perfect vehicle to set up corporate social responsibility projects.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This is what is needed in these politically turbulent times. In our fragmented world, political parties, churches and the media have lost credibility. In sport, however, people still come together. It is a tool to foster social cohesion. Therefore, I consider 50+1 to be a distinct competitive advantage for the Bundesliga.

I also welcome the fact that rules mean something in another case. Uefa is standing firm against Gianni Infantino, who recently wanted to privatise the World Cup and its profits. Along with his friend Donald Trump, he was seen by many as breaking the normal rules when Folarin Balogun’s suspension was lifted. The outcry from the global football community was loud, and it is possible that the Fifa president will fall.

When behaviour such as that in Manchester and at Fifa is punished, it is a good thing. Football must prevent questionable ideas from distancing it even further from its grassroots. Only then can it drive engagement in civil society, and only then can it strengthen Europe.

Philipp Lahm’s column was produced in partnership with Oliver Fritsch at the German online magazine Die Zeit.

Sports.title: Coach banned until 2048 for training children in DR Congo while suspended for sexual abuse
Sports.content:
A coach in the Democratic Republic of the Congo who was banned from football for 20 years by Fifa for sexual abuse of a minor has had his ban extended by five years to 2048 by the world governing body.

Jonathan Bukabakwa, known as Messi, has also been ordered to pay an additional fine of $15,000 (£11,200) after the Guardian revealed he had continued to work with young players despite his suspension.

The Congolese Association Football Federation (Fecofa) and Racing Club Baki, where Bukabakwa was coaching, have been fined $50,000 each by Fifa’s ethics committee for failing to comply with its decision to ban him for 20 years in 2023.

Quick Guide How do I 

Fecofa has also been instructed to introduce a “comprehensive education, compliance and monitoring programme for its officials, affiliated clubs and registered members” to try to ensure there is no repeat.

“The Congo DR Football Association, the club Racing Club Baki (formerly known as Esperanto FC), and the coach Jonathan Bukabakwa were found responsible for failing to comply with the decision rendered by the Fifa ethics committee on 18 October 2023,” said a Fifa statement.

Bukabakwa, who previously coached youth teams in the Limpopo and Malabo regions, was convicted of sexually abusing minors by authorities in the DRC and was released from prison last year. A Guardian investigation in August revealed there was video footage of him coaching young players at Esperanto in the Limete district of the capital, Kinshasa. Local sources confirmed he had regularly been seen taking charge of players on a school field.

Bukabakwa did not deny continuing to coach young players but claimed he had not been informed of his Fifa ban. He said he had not been questioned or received any communication from the governing body. He has denied the allegations against him.

The case has raised further questions about safeguarding in Congolese football and the ability of authorities to ensure that suspended individuals do not continue participating in the sport. Bukabakwa was provisionally suspended by Fecofa in November 2022 after media reports of alleged widespread sexual abuse in the DRC. Several other coaches were provisionally suspended at the time, although investigations into some of those other cases did not establish sufficient evidence for further action by Fecofa or Fifa.

Véron Mosengo-Omba, elected as Fecofa’s president in May, has promised to look into the previous cases once he has re-established a disciplinary committee. Fecofa was under a Fifa-appointed normalisation committee from 2023 until his election. “We will make sure that no one who is behaving like this will be involved in football in this country,” he said.

Sports.title: Ryan Bertrand leads consortium to make £87m investment in EFL club
Sports.content:
Former England defender Ryan Bertrand is leading a consortium proposing a £87m minority investment in AFC Wimbledon.

Bertrand enjoyed a 17-year career playing for the likes of Chelsea, Southampton and Aston Villa, and is now at the forefront of a group looking to acquire a stake in the League One side.

5 Ryan Bertrand made 262 Premier League appearances in his career Credit: Getty

The former full-back has teamed up with British technology expert Omar Mir, who is the sole funder of the proposed minority share buyout through investment vehicle Sloane Street Capital (SSC).

In a complicated deal, SSC are looking to pay £16m for approximately 34 per cent of the club’s shares this season.

They then plan to invest a further £71m over the next five years, at which point SSC would own 90 per cent of the club’s economic value.

AFC Wimbledon are owned by supporters in the form of the 6,265-strong Dons Trust, who currently own 50.01 per cent of the voting shares at the club - designed to ensure it remains fan-controlled.

After the Dons Trust board presented SSC's proposal to its members on Wednesday night, they will now vote on whether to accept it.

For the proposal to be approved, a 75 per cent majority is needed, with at least 50 per cent of the members voting, and that majority must account for at least 40 per cent of the total membership, with voting closing on November 17.

If the deal is successful, SSC would oversee football operations, led by Bertrand as senior football advisor, but work within budgets and processes agreed by the AFCW PLC board.

The move would also see two of SSC’s minority shareholders, investment fund boss Stuart Fiertz and sports executive Oliver Ward, joining the club’s board.

Bertrand: Wimbledon role would be an 'honour'

Bertrand, who won the Champions League, FA Cup and Europa League with Chelsea, recently discussed his hopes of being involved at Plough Lane.

He said: "AFC Wimbledon's story is unique in English football and it was built by its supporters. We felt at home from our very first meetings.

5 Bertrand started in Chelsea's 2012 Champions League final victory over Bayern Munich Credit: Getty

5 Plough Lane has been home to AFC Wimbledon since 2020 Credit: Getty

"We are not here to change what this club is. We are here to help it go further on and off the pitch, for the men's team, the women's team and the academy.

"It would be an honour to join the Wimbledon family and help write the next chapter, and we look forward to meeting members and answering their questions over the coming weeks."

Under the terms of the proposed deal, the Dons Trust voting rights would be unaffected.

They would hold veto control of the Plough Lane - known as the Cherry Red Record Stadium sponsorship reasons - freehold.

Other ideas floated as part of the potential investment include SSC taking two of the 12 seats on the club board, as well as an observer position.

Meanwhile, the Dons Trust would retain veto over the club's name, badge, colours, ground and constitution.

5 AFC Wimbledon are currently 16th in League One Credit: Getty

If SSC were to sell its stake, the Dons Trust would have first refusal and could block anyone they deem unsuitable investors.

Also included in the terms of a potential deal, SSC would see its share of AFC Wimbledon's value would stop growing immediately in the event of the consortium missing a payment.

Control would then return to the club within three months.

Earlier this year, the Dons Trust voted in favour of external investment as long as fan ownership and control were protected.

Since then, the board has considered more than 20 potential investors, with SSC emerging as the strongest.

As for Bertrand, should a deal transpire, this would represent his first venture into club ownership after retiring from football at Leicester in 2023.

5 Bertrand was capped 19 times by England, and is looking to move into football at board level Credit: Getty

Angus Fox, chair of the Dons Trust board, said of SSC's proposal: "The deal brings at least £87million into AFC Wimbledon over five years, while the Trust keeps a permanent majority of the votes, control of the Plough Lane freehold and a veto over everything that makes us who we are.

"We have set out the factors to weigh as plainly as the opportunities.

"The board recommends a yes vote, but this is our members' club and our members' decision."

Sports.title: Incredible Harry Kane underlines Ballon d’Or case by taking the mickey out of Arsenal defence
Sports.content:
Incredible Harry Kane underlines Ballon d’Or case by taking the mickey out of Arsenal defence

Harry Kane really can do it all.

The superstar striker had a hand in both of Bayern Munich's goals as they played out a pulsating 2-2 draw at home against Arsenal.

5 Kane's exploits against Arsenal earned him Player of the Match honours Credit: Getty



He assisted the Bavarians' opener with an outrageous pass that sliced through Arsenal's defence and put Alphonso Davies clear on goal.

The Canadian coolly slotted past David Raya with a first-time effort, but the plaudits for the goal belonged to Kane.

Kane's pass had Stuart Pearce in awe, so much so he felt the striker 'deserves probably half a goal' rather than being awarded the assist.

Stuart Pearce and Jim Proudfoot wax lyrical over Harry Kane

"Harry Kane, how valuable is he?" Pearce said on commentary for talkSPORT.



"What a pass that was. He's bisected, (Jurrien) Timber, who thought he covered the run, but the ball was that good. It just rolled it perfectly inside the full-back.

"Davies came onto it and opened the goal up perfectly, could take it first time.



"The weight of the pass was excellent, the direction of the pass was excellent.

"To be honest with you, Harry Kane deserves probably half a goal for that, not just an assist."



Commentator Jim Proudfoot added: "It's an absolute mickey-take of a pass."

Davies' goal cancelled out Eberechi Eze's opener in the 25th minute.

5 Kane isn't slowing down at age 33 Credit: Getty

It was then Kane's turn to get on the scoresheet from the penalty spot on the hour mark.

Kane won a spot kick attempt when his strike smacked Timber's arm inside the box, giving the referee an easy decision.



The 33-year-old stepped up and sent Raya the wrong way, with the goal marking the tenth consecutive Champions League game in which Kane had scored.

Kane is just the second player to ever achieve the feat, with Cristiano Ronaldo the first to do so.

The English superstar's goal contributions also served as a timely reminder of his qualities ahead of this year's Ballon d'Or ceremony on October 26.

Kane is considered a serious contender to take out the gong as he aims to be the first Englishman to win it since Michael Owen in 2001.



5 Kane's goal against Arsenal was his 10th for Bayern this season Credit: Getty

Harry Kane on the Ballon d'Or race

Speaking to TNT Sports after the contest, Kane wasn't overly keen on stating his case for the award but acknowledged Monday evening could be a 'special one'.

"It'd be a massive honour," Kane said.

"I've made it clear I don't like to talk about myself, but I know it'd be a massive achievement if it does happen.

"It's hard because you're right in the midst of the season, we've got so many games. Then Monday night, a big evening that could be a special one for me.



"We've got one more league game to focus and then hopefully I can enjoy the day and evening on Monday."

Unfortunately for Kane and Bayern, they could not hold on for a huge three points as Declan Rice brought Arsenal level in the 82nd minute.

5 Rice's goal ensured Arsenal avoided a first Champions League loss in normal time since May 2025 Credit: Getty

The midfielder drove into the box following a deft pass from Viktor Gyokeres and powered his effort past Manuel Neuer from close range.



Despite his late heroics, Rice was all too happy to heap praise on Kane in his post-match interview ahead of Monday's ceremony.

Declan Rice talks up Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or hopes

"For me, he's the clear winner," Rice told TNT Sports.

"I think his numbers speak for themselves. The year he's had has been remarkable. He's obviously up against some other world class players.

"When you play with him, you realise how good he is. And when you play against him, you see how much of a pain it is.

"As a striker, to play that pass that he did for that goal, and then to take the penalty how he did, he's ridiculous. He's such a good player."



5 Rice knows who he'd vote for if he could decide who won the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

Although Arsenal left Munich with a valuable point, the result came at a cost as Bukayo Saka was forced off with an injury in the tenth minute.

The winger pulled up after he attempted to play a crossfield ball and was replaced by goalscorer Eze.

Arsenal will look to return to winning ways on Saturday against Everton while Bayern travel to Freiburg on Sunday.

Sports.title: Julian Nagelsmann sounded out for Man United job with Premier League manager also a contender
Sports.content:
Julian Nagelsmann sounded out for Man United job with Premier League manager also a contender

Julian Nagelsmann has been sounded out as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick as Manchester United boss, talkSPORT understands.

Carrick is under immense pressure in the United dugout after his side were thumped 4-1 by Como in the Champions League - the latest in a string of disappointing results.



5 Nagelsmann is available after stepping down as Germany manager in the summer Credit: Getty

5 Carrick needs to turn things around at United and fast if he is to keep his job Credit: AFP

The result leaves the Red Devils without a win in seven games in all competitions, with Carrick's position in charge coming under increased scrutiny.

After the Como defeat, captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to throw the 45-year-old under the bus by criticising his tactics.



With Carrick facing calls for his short-lived reign as permanent boss to be brought to an end, United now appearing to be preparing for life without him too.

Nagelsmann leads list of candidates

Nagelsmann has emerged as a candidate to replace Carrick in recent days as speculation surrounding his future intensifies.



talkSPORT understands the former Bayern Munich manager - who is a free agent after stepping down from his role as Germany boss this summer - has admirers within the Red Devils hierarchy.

The 39-year-old was high in United's way of thinking before they opted to appoint Carrick on a permanent basis in May.



But with Nagelsmann in charge of Germany at the time, coupled with Carrick's impressive end to the season as interim boss, this meant that talks between him and United never developed.

talkSPORT also understands Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler is seen as an option by United as he has admirers at the club too.

Meanwhile, Premier League title winner Antonio Conte is prepared to take charge of United, having left Napoli in June.

The Italian's representatives have told Man United they would be keen on the role although the club is yet to express interest in him.



5 Hurzeler has overseen Brighton's impressive start to the season Credit: Getty

5 Conte has won six top flight league titles during his managerial career, including a Premier League with Chelsea Credit: AFP

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe is understood to be a candidate who could get the job easily as a free agent.

Howe was wanted by former sporting director Dan Ashworth, although minority owner Jim Ratcliffe pushed back.



Elsewhere, USA boss Mauricio Pochettino and ex-Ipswich head coach Kieran McKenna are outside contenders having been involved in previous processes.

Meanwhile, Simone Inzaghi - who guided Inter Milan to league glory and two Champions League finals - could also become available as he finds himself under pressure at Saudi side Al Hilal.

The Italian could be sacked if he fails to beat Al Qadsiah on Friday, although there is no suggestion if Man United are keen, but Inzaghi is open to a Premier League move.

Nagelsmann warning

While Nagelsmann boasts a strong CV from his time in club management at RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich, talkSPORT's Alex Crook recently warned against his appointment at Old Trafford.



5 Nagelsmann's recent struggles in international management have been highlighted as a concern Credit: Getty

Crook was unconvinced by him following his underwhelming exit from the German national team after his side crashed out of the World Cup at the round of 32 stage against Paraguay.

He questioned how the coach might handle a challenging environment at United, highlighted by recent remarks from defender Lisandro Martinez over a lack of recruitment.

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent said on the latest episode of talkSPORT's Inside Devils: "You sack another manager, you bring in someone like Nagelsmann, who didn’t cover himself in glory as the Germany boss and he’s also quite a combustible character.



"How’s he going to work with the likes of Jason Wilcox, who seemingly is going nowhere, and Omar Berrada?

"So there’s no guarantee that you change the manager and you get anything other than a short-term impact because that’s what tends to happen whenever a new manager comes in and then the players revert the type."

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes rips into Michael Carrick’s tactics in bombshell comments after Man United defeat
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has effectively thrown Michael Carrick under the bus.

The Manchester United skipper, who walked off the field shaking his head after being substituted in the 66th minute, publicly questioned Carrick's tactics immediately after a 4-1 loss to Como on Wednesday evening.

2 Fernandes didn't hold back in his verdict on Carrick's game plan Credit: Getty



What did Bruno Fernandes say about Michael Carrick?

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence," Fernandes told TNT Sports.

When pressed on whether he insinuated Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes replied: "That's on the manager and staff to see, not me.

"Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.

"As you saw with them [Como], the centre-back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.



"A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide."

Michael Carrick's response to Bruno Fernandes' scathing verdict

In response to Fernandes' comments, Carrick said: "We actually half-pressed, man-to-man in the second half and then ended up conceding a goal from that.



"There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."

Fernandes' staggering outburst comes one week after teammate Lisandro Martinez took a swipe at United technical director Jason Wilcox.



In the aftermath of United's 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid, Martinez '100 per cent expected more' from Wilcox in terms of strengthening the squad after Carrick steered them to a third-place finish last term.

Did Michael Carrick ignore his own players?

Carrick also appeared to stir controversy immediately following the Como defeat.

2 Carrick could only hold his hands up to the 700 United supporters that witnessed the 4-1 drubbing Credit: AFP

As the full-time whistle blew, Carrick ignored all of his players before making a beeline for the away end at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium.



Carrick then raised his hands in apology to the travelling supporters with strong suggestions this game could be his final act as Red Devils boss.

"I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters, they're the heartbeat of this football club and always will be," Carrick told TNT Sports.

"For them to travel, I can only apologise for the performance. Everything that they've done to get here tonight, to have to watch a performance like that, I totally feel for them.

"There's no excuses at all. I think it's just not acceptable."

Carrick also refused to be drawn on his future, which may now be on shaky ground amid a seven-game winless run.



talkSPORT understands United have already sounded out Julian Nagelsmann as a potential successor while Antonio Conte has expressed interest in taking over at Old Trafford should the axe fall on Carrick.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta gives worrying Bukayo Saka injury update as Arsenal star forced off in brutal blow
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta gives worrying Bukayo Saka injury update as Arsenal star forced off in brutal blow

Mikel Arteta is concerned about the extent of the injury Bukayo Saka sustained during Arsenal's draw against Bayern Munich.

The Gunners endured a nightmare start to their Champions League showdown in Germany when their star man went down, despite not appearing to be under any pressure.



6 Saka pulled up in pain immediately after making a pass Credit: Getty

6 The forward limped off, with Eberechi Eze replacing him Credit: Getty

With the score at 0-0, Saka pulled up after attempting to play a crossfield ball.

He immediately went to ground and indicated that he was unable to continue as medics came on to assess him.



Saka had been unchallenged when making the pass, and replays appeared to show the 25-year-old kicking the turf before clutching his thigh as he went to ground.

In a major blow to Arsenal, the winger then limped off the pitch, and was replaced by Eberechi Eze.



This marked a far from ideal start to the Champions League league phase clash, although Saka's replacement made the most of his unexpected introduction by giving Arsenal the lead on 25 minutes.

Latching onto a ball over the top, Eze rifled it into the bottom right hand corner of goal with his left foot; the goal being given after a VAR review with Eze initially being flagged offside.



This saw the England international deliver an immediate response after being hauled off at half-time in Arsenal's win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

But Arsenal's lead was short-lived, as Alphonso Davies equalised for Bayern ten minutes later.

The Canadian received an inch-perfect through ball from Ballon d'Or candidate Harry Kane before slotting past David Raya.

While the Gunners attack also took the hit via Saka’s injury, hosts Bayern were without Michael Olise and Luis Diaz from the start.



6 Eze made sure Saka's absence wasn't felt as he opened the scoring Credit: Getty

6 Davies cancelled out Arsenal's lead in an eventful first half at the Allianz Arena Credit: Getty

6 Kane got an assist and a goal on Wednesday night Credit: Getty

But they still had star striker Kane in their ranks with the former Tottenham man putting them in front with a composed penalty after Jurrien Timber blocked his goalbound shot with an arm.



The spoils were shared in Bavaria, though with Declan Rice finishing off a well-worked move to ensure Arsenal continued their unbeaten start to the season in Europe.

Arsenal are seventh in the table with seven points from a possible nine, while Bayern are 14th on five points.

Saka concern

Saka's early end to the night comes as a huge worry to both Arsenal and England.

Arteta couldn't say how long the winger will be out, revealing post-match: "They [the medical staff] are a bit concerned.



"The player having to come off feeling a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see."

6 Saka will have both club and country worried after his injury scare Credit: Getty

The Gunners star has made ten appearances in all competitions at club level this season, scoring four goals and assisting once.

But with Saka also a regular starter for England, Thomas Tuchel will be hoping his injury isn't serious enough to rule him out of the upcoming November internationals.



The Three Lions face Croatia and Spain in their final two Nations League group stage fixtures in just three weeks time.

Saka started in three of England's four games in the previous international break, and scored a double in the 7-0 thumping of Croatia.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick tipped for immediate sacking as hapless Man United humiliated by Como
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick tipped for immediate sacking as hapless Man United humiliated by Como

Manchester United's chastening 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como could well prove to be Michael Carrick's final act as manager.

This was suggested by talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook as the Red Devils floundered to a humiliating loss against the Italian side making their first ever appearance in the competition.

6 This is the biggest result in Como's history Credit: Getty

6 It's a result which could spell the end of Carrick's time as Man United boss Credit: AFP

It was a deserved result for Man United, who offered next-to-nothing going forward as well as being overrun in midfield and defence.

The three-time European champions fell behind just two minutes into the game through Nico Paz's beautiful curling effort.

Carrick's men were fortunate to get in at half time just a goal down but on a rainy evening in northern Italy the floodgates opened after the interval.

Como doubled their advantage through Anastasios Douvikas four minutes into the second half.

Paz then got his second before Jacobo Ramon rounded off a miserable game for Man United.

Joshua Zirkzee, who came on for below par Bruno Fernandes in the second half, struck in stoppage time to earn the scantest of consolation goals.

It won't represent a crumb of comfort for Carrick with pressure only increasing on the former Red Devils midfielder.

Although Crook suggested that the club will wield the axe on Carrick after this latest woe, as he said on commentary for talkSPORT: "I'm not sure Carrick's going to survive this. 4-0."

This defeat marks the first time since 2015 Man United have gone seven matches without a win.

Former Premier League player Scott Minto added: "There's nothing positive to take from this, nothing. With the ball, without the ball, they're poor both as a team and individually."

6 Man United were fortunate to get a goal in a shocking performance Credit: Getty

6

At full time, Minto added: "It's a nail in the coffin for Carrick, I feel for him."

Writing on the wall for Carrick?

After a strong interim spell in charge last term, the wheels have come off for Carrick's Man United this season.

Having lost two of their three Champions League matches this season, it's been painful on a domestic front with Man United winning just one of their seven league matches.

Meanwhile, they are already out of the Carabao Cup having lost 3-2 at home to Brighton in a match they led 2-0.

It's a divided club with defender Lisandro Martinez criticising Man United sporting director Jason Wilcox over a lack of summer investment in a bombshell interview after defeat to Atletico Madrid last week.

Martinez later confirmed positive talks with the club subsequently took place, however, there are no signs of things improving on the pitch.

6 After nine months with Carrick in the dugout, it could well be back to the coaching drawing board for Man United Credit: Getty

Up next for them is a league clash at home to Bournemouth with Man United looking to improve on their 13th-place spot in the table.

Who could succeed Carrick?

Should Carrick's time at the helm be brought to an end, United won't be short of candidates to succeed him.

talkSPORT understands former Bayern Munich manager Julian Nagelsmann - who stepped down from his role as Germany boss this summer - has admirers within the Red Devils hierarchy.

However, his appointment is one which Crook is wary of, having recently suggested he might not be up to the job after he oversaw Germany's disappointing World Cup exit.

Warning how the coach might handle a challenging environment at United, Crook told talkSPORT: "You sack another manager, you bring in someone like Nagelsmann, who didn’t cover himself in glory as the Germany boss and he’s also quite a combustible character.

"How’s he going to work with the likes of Jason Wilcox, who seemingly is going nowhere, and Omar Berrada?

6 Nagelsmann is available after stepping down as Germany manager in the summer Credit: Getty

"How’s he going to cope with what is still, I think, quite a problematic dressing room?

"So there’s no guarantee that you change the manager and you get anything other than a short-term impact because that’s what tends to happen whenever a new manager comes in and then the players revert the type."

As well as Nagelsmann, talkSPORT understands Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler is seen as an option by the club.

Meanwhile, Premier League title winner Antonio Conte is prepared to take charge of United, having left Napoli in June.

Sports.title: Kyle Walker admits to tattoo problem as he addresses Man City charges
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker has revealed one of his tattoos could be in danger if Manchester City are stripped of any league titles they won.

The City legend co-hosted Wednesday's talkSPORT Drive, where the topic turned to his former club's ongoing appeal following their guilty verdict on all charges relating to Premier League financial rule breaches.



4 Walker became one of the greatest full-backs in Premier League history at Manchester City Credit: Getty

The Premier League giants were adjudged to have artificially inflated their revenue by £900million via 'sham' contracts between 2009 and 2018.

City have since challenged their guilty verdict, insisting they are backed by a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence'.

The club won eight trophies during the period in which they are alleged to have breached financial rules, including three league titles.



It is not yet clear when and how exactly City will be punished if their appeal fails, with speculation they could be handed a huge points deduction that would ensure they spend multiple seasons in the Championship.

Also among the possible sanctions touted is the club being stripped of their titles - which would directly affect Walker.



The legendary full-back spent eight years at City from 2017 to 2025, winning 15 major trophies, including six Premier League titles.

Four of these came in historic fashion, as Pep Guardiola's side tasted consecutive league wins between the 2020/21 and 2023/24 seasons - a feat which no other Premier League side has ever achieved.



Kyle Walker's tattoo tales

As Walker's Premier League winners' medals are at risk of being taken away, he revealed exclusively on talkSPORT that this could prove extra costly to him for one spectacular reason.

That's because the England great has the words 'Four in a row', tattooed on his leg.

Asked about this by co-host Andy Goldstein, Walker confirmed: “[I've got] 'four in a row' tattooed.”

4 The first of Walker's Premier League winner's medals is threatening to be taken away Credit: Getty



Goldstein then probed: "If they take the medals away have you got a tattoo removal firm ready to take that one?"

Laughing, England and Premier League great Walker replied: “Well I'm probably going to have to do that bit!

"But you look at the likes of the great Man United squads [that won three in a row], and they never managed to get four in a row.

“So there's only a select few of us that can say that we've got four.”



He later added: "I'll try and keep it on, but hopefully we don't get things taken away."

4 Walker got inked up after City's fourth league title on the spin in the 2023/24 season Credit: Getty

4 Walker was able to joke as he admitted his tattoo soon might not be factually true Credit: talksport

Walker frank on City case

While Walker was able to see the funny side of City's potential punishment, he spoke honestly about the club's ongoing situation after launching their appeal.



Asked how he felt about the situation now, he said: “It's the big elephant in the room that we're probably all going to be asked when we're doing interviews or whatever we're doing.

“It doesn't look great. Let's not hide from the fact that they've been found guilty but they're going through an appeal.

“As a player all I can say is that all we did is go out and play our best football as a team and that I'll defend the players for the rest of my life, because I feel that what we did and what we achieved in that space of time was probably incredible and probably won't be done ever again.

“But from the outside looking in, it doesn't look great and we have to address that.”



While Premier League clubs are keen for a punishment to be delivered as soon as possible, football financial expert Stefan Borson has warned there could be delays to this amid whispers the sanction hearing will run concurrently to the club's appeal process.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk reveals Mohamed Salah’s key role in Rio Ngumoha’s development
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk has claimed that Mohamed Salah helped Rio Ngumoha's development with the teenage winger starring for Liverpool.

Ngumoha turned in a brilliant performance in the Champions League on Tuesday as the Reds beat Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield.

4 Ngumoha won the Man of the Match award for his display Credit: Getty

Ngumoha started on the right and played 74 minutes as he tore Sergi Cardona apart, including for the third Liverpool goal.

The 18-year-old charged down the wing, turned Cardona inside out and delivered it on a plate for Alexis Mac Allister.

And speaking after the game, Reds captain Van Dijk revealed that Salah and others had helped Ngumoha reach this level he is currently at.

In a post-match interview, Van Dijk said: "A few senior players [have helped him].

"I would say Cody Gakpo is definitely part of that. But everyone has that role in order to help the youngsters in the group, the players who have not had so much experience.

"Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo last year was obviously massive as Mo was one of the best wingers at the club and experienced everything so why not soak in all the information and show it on the pitch and show your own qualities?

"I think he has shown it this season but there is still much more to come.

"He's pretty electric at times and he showed it again. He was a complete threat constantly and their defender had a tough time."

Van Dijk also apologised after gifting the LaLiga side an opener.

He attempted to head a ball back to Alisson, but it dropped perfectly for Georges Mikautadze, who swivelled and converted at The Kop.

4 Van Dijk had a difficult evening personally but his sloppy play didn't cost Liverpool a win Credit: Getty

He said: "It was a terrible start.

"I think the saying is you fight an uphill battle and as a defender it is pretty difficult to come back from it. I tried but it was a bad day at the office personally but we did it together with 11 players. We turned it around and that's the main thing.

"Unfortunately, in life these things can sometimes happen. Fortunately it didn't happen too many times in my Liverpool career but tonight I was not the best. But we won and it's not about me, it's all about us. We got the three points."

Salah's mentorship role

Salah's final season might not have been his best in a Liverpool shirt, with his numbers well down. However, he adopted a role looking after Ngumoha.

And the winger revealed earlier this year what his final words were to him before Salah departed and ended up in Turkey with Trabzonspor.

Speaking about Salah's words, Ngumoha said: "The player who I probably learned the most from is Mohamed Salah, when he was at Liverpool.

4 Salah saw Ngumoha as the man to take on his mantle Credit: Getty

"He taught me a lot, especially towards the back end when he knew he was leaving. He helped me a lot.

"Like he always says about looking at his numbers and he was always telling me: 'Rio, you know you're a good player but to reach the top, you have to add the goals and assists'.

"And it will come naturally but he was just going through little things like that [with me]. When he first started [talking to me], it was like: 'Wow! I've been watching you since I was young and you're telling me how to [improve]. Like, you're helping me and you're guiding me.'

"But then over time, I saw him as a very good teammate and he was helping me a lot, so I can thank him much more."

Ngumoha's season so far

Despite the arrivals of wingers Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz, Andoni Iraola has played Ngumoha a lot.

The former Chelsea winger has featured in ever game, bar two this season in all competitions.

4 Van Dijk knows good wingers when he sees them, and he is clearly excited about Ngumoha Credit: Getty

He is yet to score a goal, but he has two assists and has appeared on the left and right for the Reds.

And with Liverpool competing on four fronts, there will be plenty more opportunities for Ngumoha.

Sports.title: 'It doesn't look good': Mikel Arteta sparks fears over Bukayo Saka injury after Arsenal winger limped off during 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
'It doesn't look good': Mikel Arteta sparks fears over Bukayo Saka injury after Arsenal winger limped off during 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta admitted he is worried about the injury suffered by winger Bukayo Saka in last night’s thrilling 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich.

Saka went off with a thigh injury just ten minutes into his team’s Champions League game with the German champions at the Allianz Arena.

Arteta said: ‘It doesn’t look good at all but we will have to wait and see.

‘They [the medical staff] are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news.’

Arsenal led through Saka’s replacement Eberechi Eze in the first-half but the brilliant Harry Kane hauled Bayern back into the game and eventually the lead with a first-half assist for Alphonso Davies and then a second-half penalty of his own.

Declan Rice grabbed an 82nd minute equaliser to send Arsenal home content but Arteta hinted that Kane – a Ballon d’Or contender ahead of next week’s ceremony in London – still sets the standards for others to follow.

Mikel Arteta has claimed that Bukayo Saka's thigh problem 'does not look good'

Saka limped off in the first half of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich on Wednesday night

‘The pass he made for the first goal, that’s the level,’ said the Arsenal manager.

England captain Kane has now scored 58 Champions League goals and is only one away from matching Cristiano Ronaldo’s record of scoring in 11 consecutive Champions League matches.

Asked by TNT about his England team-mate’s Ballon D’Or chances, Rice said: ‘He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves. The year he has had has been remarkable.

‘When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.

‘He is ridiculous, such a good player and I am lucky I can play with him, not so lucky I have to play against him.’

The injury to Saka could prove a real blow to Arteta after the winger's impressive start to the campaign in all competitions.

The England international has scored four goals in ten matches this season, while also bagging an assist in the Champions League.

However, the problem he picked up at the Allianz Arena is his latest in a string of injury issues he has faced over the last few years.

Saka admitted to playing through pain of a persistent achilles problem during Arsenal's final run-in en route to the Premier League last term. That led to limited minutes during England's World Cup campaign in the summer.

The attacker missed 15 games in all competitions last season due to the achilles issue and a hamstring problem. Saka also missed 25 games the season prior due to injury.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal: Gunners take huge step in the right direction, as Declan Rice earns point that means so much more in Mikel Arteta's bid to build dynasty
Sports.content:
A draw in Bavaria will not stand out in the list of achievements carved out stubbornly by Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal as he has taken them from nowhere to somewhere over the last six years or so. But the Arsenal manager will know what this night means, nevertheless. This is a season that must see Arsenal break fresh ground if they are to become the team we all feel they can be. They know they have questions to answer and they know what they are. They are about style and the ability to bring about repeat success. They are about building a domestic dynasty and winning things in Europe. At times Arsenal look to be quite close to that but at other times – such as in winning so drearily with one shot on target at Nottingham Forest on Sunday – they look to be rather too far away. So, yes, this felt like a big step in the right direction. An enterprising attacking performance – Arsenal could have scored four or five goals – against a team that hardly ever loses in its own stadium and then, a come from behind draw just when it seemed everything may be lost. The feeling the Arsenal team will have had when celebrating Declan Rice’s late equaliser down beneath their own fans here will have been one that should propel them forwards. Bayern are not used to teams doing that to them here and when the ball flew across Manuel Neuer and into the far corner you could feel the air being sucked out of this cavernous bowl and up into the night sky. Declan Rice smashed a powerful low effort to make it 2-2 late on against Bayern Munich Rice latched onto a through ball and his shot had too much for Manuel Neuer Harry Kane had put Bayern Munich in front from the penalty spot in the second half For Bayern had thrown their best at Arsenal here. Harry Kane had done so too. Arsenal had led midway through the first half through Eberechi Eze but as time wore on Bayern’s rapid counters threatened to become too much. Defeat beckoned. Kane – as irrepressibly as inspirational as ever – had supplied a world class assist for Alphonso Davies in the first half and then, on the hour, a penalty of his own. A loss here would have not been a disaster for Arsenal but it would have felt telling. It would have given their many critics further ammunition with which to do them down. Not good enough in Europe. Flat track bullies. Stuck in the mud. Not moving forwards. So it was a good night for Arsenal if not a perfect one. An injury to Bukayo Saka, for example, was not on Arteta’s wish list. He was clipped from behind in the tenth minute and went down holding the back of his knee. That was the end of his evening and the injury will be a worry. The only consolation to Arteta will have been that his replacement took his opportunity. This has not been a stellar season for Eze but you would not have known it watching him drive a pass from Martin Odegaard across Manuel Neuer and in to the far corner with his left foot in the 25th minute. The supply from Odegaard was exemplary but it needed a finish to match. At that point, Arsenal were worth the lead, even if Bayern had attacked on the counter to good effect. Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya had to save sharply from Serge Gnabry after one such break while a lofted Kane pass a couple of minutes before Eze’s goal could have led to something had Ismael Saibari not applied such a clumsy touch. Arsenal, meanwhile, had their own moments to ponder. Twice from corners they had opportunities at the far post but Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes couldn’t take them. Alphonso Davies equalised for the German side with a tidy finish past David Raya Eberechi Eze fired a composed effort past Manuel Neuer to break the deadlock in Munich After a slow start, it had become a good game. Arsenal were purposeful and ambitious if a little too square across the back at times. Eventually, they were caught out. Kane’s pass inside Jurrien Timber from just inside the Arsenal half could not have been more geometrically perfect had he used a set square and Davies ran on to open his body and beat Raya quite comfortably. Kane’s goal – his 58th in the competition – was eventually to arrive on the hour and arrived after a spell of Bayern pressure. Before that, though, Arsenal had another couple of huge moments. Almost immediately after half-time, Neuer produced a stunning save to push a Gabriel header up on to the crossbar from another corner. At the other end Raya denied Dayot Upamecano in similarly brilliant fashion. It was an increasingly engaging game but one that Bayern were beginning to enjoy rather more. Their forays into the attacking third had become more regular and brought with them a greater menace. Kane, for his part, was showcasing his full repertoire, spending as much time in deep position as he was through the middle. There were concerning scenes for the Gunners when Saka limped off early on in the game This was a draw worth far more than the solitary point for Mikel Arteta's side But he was in the right place on the hour to meet a cross from Konrad Laimer and when his shot struck the sprawling Jurrien Timber on the arm a penalty was the only decision available. Kane took it and, after a little stutter, slotted it to Raya’s right with the keeper committed in the other direction. Bayern almost sealed the game soon after only for Laimer’s right foot shot to miss Raya’s right hand post. So Arsenal remained in it and – with Viktor Gyokeres on to change the shape of their attacks – they eventually took what they deserved. The move down the right side was slick and Rice’s finish – after a one-two with the big striker – was perfect, across Neuer with power. The celebrations that followed were about much more than a single Champions League point. NOW READ: Bayern Munich v Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars left the Gunners defence exposed too often? Who pulled the strings for Mikel Arteta's men? And who had a 'quiet' night?

Sports.title: Bayern Munich v Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars left the Gunners defence exposed too often? Who pulled the strings for Mikel Arteta's men? And who had a 'quiet' night?
Sports.content:
Declan Rice stole the limelight from Harry Kane as Arsenal hit back to snatch a thrilling 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in a heavyweight Champions League clash at the Allianz Arena.

Gunners midfielder Rice lashed low beyond Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer eight minutes from time to extend his side’s unbeaten start to this season’s competition following back-to-back wins over Napoli and Lille.

Kane was on course to claim the winner after registering his 16th goal in 23 career outings against Arsenal by converting a 61st-minute penalty following Jurrien Timber’s handball.

The England captain earlier produced a sublime assist for Alphonso Davies to cancel out Eberechi Eze’s opener.

But in their biggest test since losing last season’s final to Paris St Germain on penalties, Mikel Arteta’s Premier League champions responded well to deservedly return home with a share of the spoils.

Here ISAAN KHAN rates Arsenal's top performers on the night.

David Raya - 7

Top save to deny Dayot Upamecano from point-blank range. Impressive with his fast distribution to kickstart counter-attacks.

Jurrien Timber - 4

Out of position for Alphonso Davies’ goal and caught out throughout the match. Conceded a penalty for a handball following Harry Kane's strike.

Jurrien Timber endured a difficult night and was caught out of position for Bayern's opener

Ezri Konsa - 5

Tasked with keeping tabs on Kane, yet the England man found ways to find space. A couple of strong, important blocks, but his positioning ought to be better.

Gabriel - 6

Strong at the back and up for the fight. Stepped up when required, not deterred by the task at hand.

Riccardo Calafiori - 5

A constant threat in the final third but, like his fellow full back Timber, he left the backline exposed too often.

Martin Odegaard - 8

Pulled the strings for Arteta's side and played some classy passes, including a sublime assist for Eberechi Eze. The Norwegian is hard to stop when he’s in this mood.

Martin Odegaard delivered another impressive display as the Arsenal captain rediscovers his best form

Declan Rice - 8

Energetic in the middle of the park and covered lots of ground. His corner-kicks caused havoc in the Bayern area and struck a well-taken goal.

Bruno Guimaraes - 6

All-action display. Put in a number of crucial challenges and was a threat going forwards. Had a header well-saved by Manuel Neuer.

Bukayo Saka - 5

Pulled up with what looked like a quad injury in the opening 10 minutes, signalling to the bench that he would not be able to continue. Massive blow for Arsenal, who will be sweating over the severity of Saka's blow.

Kai Havertz - 4

A quiet night with the German unable to create openings in threatening areas.

It was a quiet night for Kai Havertz, who struggled to make an impact

Noni Madueke - 5

Direct and tried to make things happen. Thoese opportunities dwindled in the second-half as Bayern grabbed control of the tie.

Substitutions:

Eberechi Eze - 7

Deserves credit after an impressive, goalscoring cameo following recent scrutiny.

Viktor Gyokeres - 7

Myles Lewis-Skelly - 6

Manager: Mikel Arteta - 7

A good move to bring on Viktor Gyokeres, who came off the bench to assist Rice. Will be pleased to walk away with a point.

Boss Mikel Arteta will be pleased with his side's performance and the point gained in Germany

BAYERN MUNICH (4-2-3-1): Neuer 7; Laimer 6, Upamecano 7, Min-Jae 6 (Tah 6, 46mins), Stanisic 6; Pavlovic 6, Bischof 6; Gnabry 6 (Karl 68, 6), Saibari 6 (Diaz 6, 68), Davies 8; Kane 8.

Referee: Davide Massa - 6

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag reveals failed plot to reunite with Alejandro Garnacho at Leverkusen as ex-Man United boss admits out-of-sorts star is a 'little bit selfish' and 'needs love' amid Aston Villa exile
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag reveals failed plot to reunite with Alejandro Garnacho at Leverkusen as ex-Man United boss admits out-of-sorts star is a 'little bit selfish' and 'needs love' amid Aston Villa exile

Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has leapt to the defence of Alejandro Garnacho, revealing he tried to sign the winger during his ill-fated spell at Bayer Leverkusen.

Garnacho made his transition from United's academy into the first-team under Ten Hag with the Dutchman handing him his debut. Their time together peaked in the 2024 FA Cup final 2-1 win over Manchester City with Garnacho scoring the opening goal.

Ten Hag was sacked as United boss in October 2024, before returning to management with Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025. However, he lasted only two Bundesliga matches before he was dismissed - a Bundesliga record.

The 56-year-old's fortunes since that FA Cup final win mirror that of Garnacho who was sold to Chelsea for £40million in August 2025. He only lasted a season at the Blues after underwhelming before joining Aston Villa on loan, where he is down the pecking order of manager Unai Emery.

But speaking about Garnacho, Ten Hag labelled him as an 'amazing player' who can do 'incredible things', but warned to get the best out of him he has to remain disciplined.

'I regret where he is now. I told him, "Come to Leverkusen". But luckily he didn't. He wanted to stay in England. I understand, the best league, so he denied,' he told The Athletic of an attempt to sign the Argentine in the summer of 2025 before he joined Chelsea.

Erik ten Hag (right) has spoken highly about Alejandro Garnacho after their time at Man United

Now at Aston Villa on loan from Chelsea, the winger has struggled for first-team minutes so far

'He's a character, you have to manage him, but I had a strong connection with him.

'But it's also up to him, of course, but he needs a coach, a particular coach, who will give him trust, who will give him love. He needs the love, definitely. But he's an amazing player. What's so special about him is he can run all day, high volume at really high speed, all game, back and forward.

'Sometimes his head is not on defending. So mentally, his mindset, you have to make sure he is focused and disciplined and does the job every transition, but he's capable of doing it and attacking-wise he can go forward and do incredible things, making dribbles, finishing. He can do the final pass, but sometimes he's a little bit selfish but you balance this.'

Since joining Aston Villa on loan, Garnacho has only made four substitute appearances for a total of 42 minutes.

His last appearance under Emery came in the 6-0 win over Fenerbahce in the Europa League on October 15 - where he came on with 11 minutes remaining.

Despite that cameo, the 22-year-old was omitted from their matchday squad for Saturday's 2-1 victory at Newcastle United. He hasn't played in the Premier League since his substitute appearance in a 0-0 draw at Hull City on September 5.

Ten Hag's thoughts on his former United player comes after he revealed his frustration at the club's hierarchy's decision to sell Scott McTominay to Napoli for £25m in the summer of 2024 against his wishes.

'They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn't keep.'

Keeping McTominay at Old Trafford was one of those promises, according to Ten Hag.

The Scot was sold to Napoli for £25million in the summer of 2024 and has since gone on to become one of the top midfielders in Italy, becoming a fan favourite at the Serie A club after steering them to the title in his first season.

He even earned a Ballon d'Or nomination and was compared to Argentina icon Diego Maradona by adoring Napoli fans.

On McTominay, Ten Hag said: 'That's why I got disappointed. In Ibiza, we agreed. I said, "No selling Scott McTominay". We would go aligned in the transfer window.

'I make an argument, a reason: we don't have scoring abilities. Scott brings scoring abilities and great mentality. He has United in all his veins. So when they bring up the subject, "No". And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.'

McTominay's transfer to Napoli was used by United's chiefs to raise funds for £42m midfielder Manuel Ugarte, who has struggled to impress since his arrival.

The Uruguayan, who is currently out injured with an anterior cruciate ligament tear he suffered at the World Cup, was mostly used as a squad player under Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick last season.

Sports.title: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes questions Michael Carrick's tactics in wake of Champions League humiliation in Como - after boss was left 'angry' by team's display and apologised to supporters
Sports.content:
Man United captain Bruno Fernandes questions Michael Carrick's tactics in wake of Champions League humiliation in Como - after boss was left 'angry' by team's display and apologised to supporters

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Michael Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the club’s Champions League humiliation in Como.

United were humbled 4-1 as their wretched season hit a new low and Carrick, who expressed his 'anger' at the performance, suffered his fifth defeat in 11 games.

A week after Lisandro Martinez had taken aim at his Old Trafford bosses – and director of football Jason Wilcox in particular – Fernandes broke ranks to question why United were so passive again.

He said: ‘It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.’

Asked if he meant that Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: ‘That's on the manager and staff to say, not me.

‘Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with Como, the centre back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to hit out at manager Michael Carrick

Fernandes expressed his frustration after Carrick's side were thrashed 4-1 by Como

‘A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide.’

Having conceded to Atletico after 50 seconds last week, United were behind within two minutes as Como star Nico Paz struck the first of his two goals.

‘It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early,’ said Fernandes. ‘Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.

‘Conceding early makes us go into game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.’

Fernandes was surprisingly substituted by Carrick midway through the second half, and the United skipper shook his head in frustration as he made his way back to the dugout.

Carrick refused to be drawn on Fernandes' post-match outburst but admitted he was left 'angry' by his team's performance in Italy.

He said: 'I'm angry to be honest. My whole life is wrapped around this. I didn't like what I've seen tonight.'

Carrick added: 'There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win.'

On their performance more widely, the former United midfielder said: 'It was more than disappointing. I think everyone has to take responsibility for that.

'I'll 100 per cent take responsibility for the overall team and performance; that stops with me and I accept that. But as a supporter of this club for so long and I care so much about this club, to see a performance like that is unacceptable.

'A lot of it is the motivation, intensity and purpose you have to bring in a game of football and we didn't bring that today. You can't turn it on and off or choose when you perform or give absolutely everything. Until you do that you're not going to win enough football matches.'

Fernandes was substituted in the second half and looked frustrated as he left the pitch

Carrick apologised to United's travelling fans after the match and held his hands up in their direction having marched across the pitch, before he repeated this stance when speaking to the media.

He added: 'I care an unbelievable amount about these supporters. They're the heartbeat of this football club and always will be.

'For them to travel, I have to apologise for the performance and everything they've done to get here tonight. To watch a performance like that I feel for them. There's no excuses for that and it's totally unacceptable.'

Sports.title: Aston Villa's new-look team continue to make strides as Unai Emery shows why he is one of the world's great managers after 3-1 win over Viking, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Aston Villa's new-look team continue to make strides as Unai Emery shows why he is one of the world's great managers after 3-1 win over Viking, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Two questions sprang to mind on a night of contrasting fortunes for Premier League clubs in the Champions League.

First, why have Manchester United never made a concerted attempt to bring in Unai Emery as manager? And even if they did, why on Earth would the Aston Villa boss choose to move to Old Trafford right now?

Emery is approaching his fourth anniversary in charge at Villa Park. He took over with the club on the fringes of a relegation battle and since then, he has led them to Champions League qualification twice, as well as lifting the Europa League last season.

Not long after United had fallen apart at Como, Emery was guiding Villa to their third straight victory in the season’s Champions League.

Ross Barkley’s header and Emi Buendia’s penalty made it 2-0 at half-time, and the excellent Alysson’s cross flew in off Henrik Heggheim for the third goal. Peter Christiansen replied late on for Viking.

Aston Villa thumped Norwegian side Viking 3-1 in the Champions League at Villa Park

The comfortable victory took Unai Emery's side to joint-top of the league phase standings

Villa are joint-top of the league phase with a maximum nine points, which was good enough to reach the play-off round in some cases last term. There are 15 points still to play for.

While United have moved from one baffling appointment to another, sacking Erik ten Hag to hire Ruben Amorim and then replacing the Portuguese with Michael Carrick, Emery has been right under their noses.

But they never made a serious bid to poach the Premier League’s best pound-for-pound manager and if that boat has now sailed, it would serve them right.

Aston Villa’s Alex Ferguson

In terms of the control he has, Emery is the closest there is to Ferguson in the modern Premier League.

Few managers’ influence stretches across a club as Emery’s does and just like Ferguson, Emery is showing he is comfortable with dismantling a successful team and rebuilding it.

Villa lost six players who started last season’s Europa League final and their prospects were uncertain. When Emery’s men were hammered at Brighton on the opening day of the season, it seemed they may have changed too much too soon.

Not a bit of it. There will still be bumps in the road, but already Johan Manzambi – absent here – looks one of the signings of the summer, as does Nicolas Jackson.

Ibrahim Mbaye will only improve, Joao Gomes is growing into his role and now Leon Goretzka is fully fit, he will surely have a significant contribution to make, while Alysson is coming to the boil nicely. Zion Suzuki looks an ideal replacement for Emi Martinez in goal.

There are still some doubts about the defence in Ezri Konsa’s absence but Villa’s attacking options are the envy of most across Europe.

Villa's new-look side is starting to come together despite a significant summer overhaul

Underestimated Emery

Despite winning 12 major trophies, Emery still does not receive the recognition he deserves in some quarters.

According to one live blog, BBC summariser and former England defender Matthew Upson described Emery as ‘a safe pair of hands for any club’.

Safe pair of hands? Seriously? With all respect, we are talking about one of the world’s great managers, not someone hired to steer a relegation-threatened side to mid-table.

Emery has coached some of the world’s best players and even improved them. Working under Emery, Youri Tielemans was one of the league’s best midfielders last season. Just look at him now as he struggles under a vastly inferior coach at United.

Emery is comfortably the best-paid employee at Villa. His annual salary of about £15million puts him in the top bracket of world managers and they think him worth every penny.

Unai Emery continues to work wonders and he is one of the world's greatest managers

The odd man out

Alejandro Garnacho continues to have a confusing time at Villa Park. The former United winger, on loan from Chelsea, was a late substitute here and looked lively.

He has yet to start a game though and doubts remain about how much Villa really want him.

The Argentine may start in the Carabao Cup at Bournemouth next week but barring an unexpected series of events, it seems unlikely his £43m permanent move will be triggered. January promises to be interesting for him.

But Alejandro Garnacho is having a confusing time at Villa Park and his future looks uncertain

Sports.title: Como 4-1 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars fare worst in our most damning ratings EVER after Michael Carrick's side sink to new low?
Sports.content:
Things went from bad to worse at Manchester United as their 'fresh start' under Michael Carrick began with a disastrous 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Como.

In the pouring rain, United capitulated under the pressure put on by Cesc Fabregas' young guns and they were behind inside two minutes in what was the start of a very long evening.

Anastasios Douvikas got himself on the scoresheet, teed up by man of the match Nico Paz, who scored twice, before Jacobo Ramon compounded United's misery with a fourth.

By the time Joshua Zirkzee held his run to stay onside to score a consolation in stoppage time, there was barely a flicker of a smile on the faces of anyone wearing United white.

At that stage, United's wounded supporters had long left in their droves, furious at a performance that suggests this United group are only heading in one direction: backwards.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT gives his verdict on a truly hapless Manchester United performance in Italy...

Manchester United have a lot of soul searching to do after a shambolic defeat to Como

Nico Paz ran United ragged with a brace and an assist as United's season gets even worse

Manchester United (4-2-3-1)

Senne Lammens – 4

What is he meant to do when those in front of him are so hopeless? The defence was about as solid as a house of cards in a gentle breeze. Genuinely hopeless and as long as that continues, Lammens is on a hiding to nothing.

Diogo Dalot – 3

Wasted a golden opportunity after a deflection fell at his feet in the box, shooting a whisker wide of the post. That proved costly when Como scored less than a minute later. Works hard and was willing at right back, where he started, and left back, where he went at half time. Some at United feel Dalot is unfairly criticised when the chips are down, but he was miles away from the required quality here.

Matthijs de Ligt – 3

His first United appearance in 325 days and there was so much hope that the Dutchman could pick up where he left off. The positive is that he came through it unscathed. By the time he went off, it was a disastrous night for United and De Ligt was far from blameless after losing sight of Douvikas before stumbling as Como made it 2-0.

Harry Maguire – 4

Made a super last-ditch, sliding challenge to deny a second goal but it all proved in vain. Maguire called out the team for not showing enough bravery away to Leeds and this as a response was disastrous.

He was the best of the back-line but that's not saying much. Looks one of very few who can actually handle the pressure and navigate the storm now.

Harry Maguire called out the bravery of this team after Leeds and it didn't have any impact

Noussair Mazraoui – 3

Ran ragged at both left back, where he started, and at right back, where he played in the second half. It was Mazraoui who was at fault for Leeds' equaliser at the weekend and his press to close out in the lead up to Como's second goal was dreadful. Looked like a rabbit in headlights by the time Kaiki, gifted the freedom of Como by Mazraoui, crossed in for the hosts' fourth.

Mason Mount – 3

Has won this competition and has plenty of experience at the level but looked way short of the necessary quality required as this youthful Como team made him look distinctly average. Constantly came out second best in duels.

Andrey Santos – 4

Found himself completely overrun in the middle of the park – he wasn't alone in that – and was hooked at half-time after a rash slide to bring down Nico Paz brought a yellow card. Never got close to the speed of the game. The fact it was only 1-0 when he went off goes in his favour.

Bryan Mbeumo – 4

Has looked best at centre forward and so, naturally, he was deployed wide off the right, a position he doesn't ever seem to thrive in. Made a couple of smart runs but chances were at a premium and he was marginalised.

Bryan Mbeumo was pushed out on to the right and it massively limited what he is good at

Youri Tielemans – 4

Keeps starting matches but this one was one where it was easy to forget he was playing. Totally anonymous.

Matheus Cunha – 3

Another who was totally anonymous. Had one touch in the Como box, didn't create a single chance, and had just one shot off target before he was hooked at half-time alongside Santos. Been in and out of the side of late and this didn't do anything to improve his odds of more starts.

Bruno Fernandes – 4

Shook his head as he was taken off just after an hour into this one-sided contest but the truth is his performances have been way below the levels he has previously shown he can reach and he could have few complaints at coming off.

This false-nine experiment they have used in the past two games isn't yielding successful results.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 2

Spoke about a 'fresh start' after the draw at Leeds and then saw his side get totally dominated by a quicker, hungrier and better coached team. This was alarming mostly because United never looked remotely threatening, never mind threatening to pull off a positive result.

Michael Carrick is going to be under enormous pressure now as he bids to keep his job

SUBS

Amad (for Matheus Cunha, 46min) – 6

The brightest player in a United shirt. Looked to actually make stuff happen, and it was his ball in to Zirkzee that led to the late consolation.

Carlos Baleba (for Andrey Santos, 46) – 5

Catastrophic error to concede possession to Nico Paz as he broke to score a third. Did at least add some physicality that is severely lacking in this team. United cannot start matches going forward without him.

Joshua Zirkzee (for Bruno Fernandes, 67)

Scored in what was basically the only positive on a sobering night. Ended his drought.

Harry Amass (for Matthijs de Ligt, 79)

Shea Lacey (for Bryan Mbeumo, 86)

Como (4-2-3-1)

Butez 6; Couto 7, Ramon 7, Kempf 6, Valle 6; Milla 7, Perrone 8; Da Cunha 7, Paz 9 (Ricci 80), Baturina 7 (Caqueret 64, 7); Douvikas 8

Goals: Paz (2, 57), Douvikas (49), Ramon (76)

Manager: Cesc Fabregas 8
