Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Are you going to the United States Grand Prix?

If you’re heading to USA for this weekend’s race, we want to hear from you:

Who do you think will be the team to beat in the United States Grand Prix? Have your say below.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Claims Floyd Mayweather Title Fight Agreement
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia claims he and Floyd Mayweather have agreed to fight for the WBC welterweight title, putting a championship label on a matchup that looks more like a celebrity event than serious business at 147.

The selling point is obvious: Garcia gets a chance to put the first loss on Mayweather’s professional record. Whether beating a 49-year-old version of Floyd would prove much about Ryan’s ability is another question.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,” Garcia posted on X. “But it’s real Floyd and I agree to a fight.”

Garcia added: “147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world. 50-0 vs The current champ.”

That is Garcia announcing an agreement. His post does not provide a date, venue, or broadcaster, and it does not establish that the WBC has approved Mayweather as a title challenger. Those details still need to follow before this can be treated as a confirmed championship fight.

As a commercial idea, it is easy to understand. Mayweather’s undefeated record gives the promotion something to sell beyond the usual exhibition routine. Ryan would be chasing the “0,” while Floyd would be selling the possibility that he can still beat a much younger champion.

As a title defense, it is a circus.

Mayweather’s reputation was earned against elite fighters over a long career. That reputation does not tell us what he can do at 49 against a current welterweight champion. Putting his record on the line would make the result official, but it would not turn back the clock.

Garcia would also leave himself open to an obvious criticism. Beat Floyd, and he has beaten a retired great approaching 50. Struggle with him, and the questions about Ryan become considerably louder.

There will be people willing to buy it. Two famous names and the possibility of Mayweather finally losing are enough to draw attention beyond boxing’s regular audience.

That is the appeal Garcia is selling. The WBC belt adds decoration, but the attraction is celebrity, money, and a famous unbeaten record.

Sanctioning this as an official WBC welterweight title defense would make a complete joke of the belt and freeze out actual contenders at 147. If two massive names want an unsanctioned exhibition to generate huge pay-per-view numbers, boxing fans understand the drill.

Celebrity events happen all the time now. Slapping an authentic world championship onto it crosses the line from entertainment into parody. Mayweather turns 50 next February and has not fought in a sanctioned professional bout since 2017. He is not ranked by the WBC.

Handing him an immediate shot at a real crown purely because of his fame insults every active fighter grinding through eliminators for a mandatory spot. For Garcia, putting the belt up brings zero boxing credit. If he blows out a 49-year-old retired legend, nobody takes it seriously as a legitimate championship victory.

If he looks bad or gets touched up by Floyd, critics will tear him apart. Keeping it as an exhibition protects the credibility of the sanctioning body, keeps the division moving, and lets fans enjoy the spectacle for what it really is. Turning it into an official title fight cheapens the entire sport.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Could Fight Four Times In 2027
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma could box four times in 2027, with promoter Frank Warren targeting a January return to give the heavyweight an early start on a busy year.

Warren wants at least three appearances, though fitting in a fourth will depend on the opposition. No opponent or venue has been announced for Itauma’s next fight.

“I would like him to have a minimum of three fights, maybe four if we can fit them in, depending on the opposition as well, of course,” Warren told BoxNation.

That last qualification leaves room for the schedule to change. Four fights would give Itauma regular work, but the value of that activity will come from who Warren puts in front of him. An opponent who makes him solve different problems could provide more than another quick finish.

Warren expects to reveal the next step shortly.

“I think we’ll be sometime next week, towards the end of next week, announcing something, but he’ll be fighting very early next year, probably in January,” he said.

January remains a target rather than a confirmed booking. Still, getting Itauma out that early would leave Warren enough room to spread three more appearances across the remainder of 2027, provided the fights and recovery periods allow it.

The opponent announcement will tell us more about the ambition behind that schedule. Warren offered no names and made no commitment to a world title fight during this interview. His comments were about getting Itauma into the ring regularly.

There is also a practical balance to find. As the opposition improves, fights can require longer preparation and leave less room for a quick turnaround. Warren’s preference for three, with four possible, gives him flexibility without committing Itauma to dates before the opponents are secured.

A busy calendar is a reasonable starting point. The next question is whether those appearances move Itauma closer to the heavyweights he eventually needs to beat.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol vs Callum Smith Gets DAZN Confirmation
Sports.content:
DAZN has officially confirmed its coverage of Dmitry Bivol’s December 12 title defense against Callum Smith in Yekaterinburg, Russia, where the Briton will challenge for the WBA, IBF and WBO light heavyweight belts.

The fight was announced on October 12, with DAZN already identified as the broadcaster. Wednesday’s promotional post provides the platform’s own confirmation, although it adds no new date, venue or opponent.

“An unmissable world title unification between Dmitry Bivol & Callum Smith lands on DAZN,” the broadcaster posted.

Bivol will defend his three belts at the UMMC Arena against Smith, who gets an opportunity to become a two-division world champion. Winning those titles requires solving a difficult boxing puzzle on the champion’s home turf.

Smith’s power gives him a threat if he can get close enough to use it. Bivol’s footwork and quick combinations can leave opponents losing rounds while trying to get into punching position. Smith cannot afford to follow him around without producing enough offense.

His prolonged absence has also taken some of the interest out of this fight. Smith’s February 2025 victory over Joshua Buatsi gave him something to build on, but fans will have waited almost 22 months to see him fight again by December 12.

That layoff was not entirely by choice. Smith was scheduled to defend his WBO interim title against David Morrell on April 18 in Liverpool before a training camp injury forced him out less than two weeks before the event. The fight never happened.

The injury explains the canceled return, but it cannot restore the attention lost during his absence. The Buatsi victory has faded into the background, leaving Smith without a recent performance to get fans talking about his chances against Bivol.

There is a sporting cost, too. Smith must find his timing against a champion who can score and move before an opponent gets his punches off. Spending several rounds settling in could leave the challenger chasing a substantial lead.

DAZN has confirmed where fans can watch. Smith’s task is to make this competitive after spending so long out of the ring.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Ready As Teofimo Lopez Deadline Hits Tomorrow
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall has made it known he is ready to get down to business with the October 22 deadline running out for talks on his ordered WBA welterweight title fight against Teofimo Lopez.

The British southpaw went onto social media while waiting to see if he lands his mandatory crack or gets hit with another postponement.

“READY FOR A FIGHT,” Catterall posted, tagging DAZN Boxing to make sure the network heard him loud and clear.

That puts Catterall’s stance out there in four words. He wants an official date on the calendar, yet the WBA process has not produced one.

Teofimo’s side has tried to get special permission to go after a different opponent, looking into a massive unification clash against Ryan Garcia for early 2027. Catterall stands as the main roadblock for that route because the WBA already issued the order for its super champion to face him next.

Catterall picked up the WBA regular title by beating Shakhram Giyasov back in May. Grabbing that strap put him in direct position for the bout he is trying to nail down right now. Five months have gone by, and he finds himself still stuck waiting for that mandatory pathway to deliver an actual ring return.

The deadline hits at the close of business Eastern Time on Thursday, October 22. It represents the conclusion of the official discussion window set up by the WBA, not an automatic guarantee that Teofimo gets stripped on the spot.

The pending appeal keeps Catterall hanging around for a ruling that will dictate who he faces and how quickly he gets back under the lights. He recently talked about his career being stalled out, and his latest message makes it obvious that no agreement came together behind closed doors.

There is a huge cash reason for Teofimo to chase Ryan Garcia instead. That matchup pulls in massive public interest compared to a mandatory chore against Catterall. Still, Catterall followed every single sanctioning body rule to earn his spot, and a giant commercial payday for the champion does nothing to restore the lost months Catterall spent on the shelf.

Sports.title: Brandon Figueroa’s Team Believed 75% Would Beat Kameda
Sports.content:
Brandon Figueroa’s corner figured a three-quarters version of their fighter could still handle Tomoki Kameda. Instead of an easy night, pushing through a wrecked training camp produced a blown scale reading along with a scrapped title defense.

How they talked themselves into that position tells the real story. They watched Kameda struggle against Angelo Leo, convincing themselves they had spotted an opponent Figueroa could overpower on cruise control. Counting on an opponent’s flaws while dragging a hurt fighter through a brutal cut was asking for trouble from day one.

Chris Mannix outlined that logic after sitting down with Figueroa alongside trainer Manny Robles during fight week. According to Mannix, the team rolled the dice on the belief that a seventy-five percent Figueroa could handle a fully prepared Kameda. Robles pointed directly to Kameda hesitating to let his hands go against Leo as justification. Spotting flaws in Kameda did nothing to heal Figueroa’s compromised body.

“They took a calculated risk that they believed that 75% of Brandon Figueroa was going to be good enough to beat 100% of Tomoki Kameda,” said Mannix on his channel.

Sergio Mora painted a grim scene from the hotel. Figueroa looked completely drained, showing sunken cheeks alongside zero energy in his voice. Mora also picked up zero real belief from the camp members standing around him.

Those details leave the team with little defense. This went beyond routine fight-week sluggishness. Their own timeline showed an injury disrupting preparation, followed by an obvious physical collapse trying to make the limit.

Mora mentioned Tim Bradley stepping up to challenge the room, asking them directly why they were walking toward the ring while compromised. Bradley told them bluntly that no purse justifies risking long-term health. Mora suspected Bradley played a major part in talking them off the ledge, even if that remains his personal read on the room.

Purses drove the train too. Mora noted the team nodded in agreement when he brought up walking away from guaranteed money. Mannix pointed out another worry, specifically that Figueroa lacked any guarantee about landing another broadcast date anytime soon.

Uncertainty explains the pressure. It still fails to justify putting a fighter in harm’s way.

Kameda did his job, locked in his weight, then watched his title shot vanish on fight morning. Figueroa completely dumped the momentum built from stopping Nick Ball.

Pulling the plug was the only acceptable move once Figueroa broke down. The heat belongs squarely on the days leading up to it, when his corner treated Kameda’s flaws as an excuse to ignore their own fighter’s reality.

Figueroa blew the biggest payday of his career in the process. Keeping that belt would have placed him directly in the crosshairs for Naoya Inoue’s planned jump to featherweight in 2027. Holding a world title gave him the one bargaining chip the Japanese star actually needs.

That belt was Figueroa’s golden ticket. Facing Kameda was simply supposed to be the routine checkpoint to keep him in line for the jackpot.

Instead, he walked out of Las Vegas with an empty bank account, no strap, plus a ruined argument for landing Inoue. While that clash was never locked in stone, tossing the hardware away stripped Inoue’s handlers of any reason to look his way.

That reality turns the corner’s gamble into pure negligence. Figueroa’s team got tunnel vision worrying if a three-quarters version could slide past Kameda, completely blind to what blowing the scale would cost down the road.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Expects Less Volume From Vergil Ortiz
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman is already spinning Vergil Ortiz Jr. as a more manageable problem than Sebastian Fundora, which tells you everything about how veteran fighters rationalize dangerous matchups.

Thurman is betting that a drop in incoming punches equates to breathing room. Trading Fundora’s exhausting, awkward flurries for Ortiz’s firepower is a terrible bargain.

Fundora drowned Thurman in non-stop punches, but Ortiz does not need triple-digit punch outputs to ruin someone’s night. He sits down on every single delivery, cuts off escape routes, and forces opponents into survival mode.

“Virgil might be holding back his volume, but his power is going to be more intense,” Thurman told MillCity Boxing. “So, once again, it’s dangerous.”

Thurman talking about Ortiz holding back volume sounds like wishful thinking from a fighter trying to talk himself into believing he will get space to operate. He even tries to compare the transition to his past fights against Shawn Porter and Danny Garcia. Porter brought a relentless dogfight, while Garcia offered pauses between exchanges that allowed Thurman to reset his feet.

“I think he’s going to be easier to match the volume, the two-punch combos, the three-punch combos,” Thurman said.

The fatal flaw in that logic is simple: Garcia let fighters off the hook. Ortiz hunts. Those quiet moments Thurman thinks he will exploit between short combinations will not be rest periods. They will be traps where Ortiz walks him into the ropes and forces him to backpedal under heavy artillery.

At 37, Thurman’s legs look gone compared to his prime. He used to circle the perimeter, plant his feet, fire a quick combination, and skip out of range before anyone could touch him. Against Fundora, he had no snap left to hold his ground, which is why he spent from rounds 3 to 6 of that fight purely in track-and-field mode.

If Thurman refuses to sit down on his shots, Ortiz Jr. will walk through him. A dangerous puncher only respects what is coming back at him. The moment Ortiz Jr. realizes Thurman is strictly on his bicycle and throwing nothing to deter him, he will pin his ears back, cut off the ring, and trap Thurman on the ropes. Without pop on his punches to gain Ortiz’s respect, running just delays the inevitable while draining Thurman’s dwindling gas tank.

The threat of a referee stoppage is very real here. Against Fundora, Thurman reached a point where he was offering zero offensive resistance, and ringside officials will step in every time if a guy looks like target practice and shows no intention of fighting back.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Backs Tyson Fury To Stop Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Frank Warren is convinced Tyson Fury stops Anthony Joshua inside the distance, pinpointing AJ’s defensive lapses during his own offensive bursts as the decisive flaw.

Fury’s timing and counterpunching remain central to Warren’s prediction. The promoter views the dynamic much like he viewed Daniel Dubois’s upset win over Joshua, even while admitting neither man is operating at their athletic peak.

“Styles make fights. I believe the same as I believed Daniel, when he fought AJ, he would knock him out and beat him. I think Tyson would do the same thing,” Warren said to Sky Sports Boxing. “I just feel that Tyson has his number, in my opinion. Maybe wrong. The one thing about AJ, as we all know, he can whack.”

Warren’s logic involves the split second Joshua commits to his combinations. While Joshua’s power creates danger whenever he fires, his delayed guard gives an elite counterpuncher clear targets before his hands return home.

“When he throws his shots, he leaves himself very vulnerable, and Tyson’s a good counterpuncher,” Warren added.

Capitalizing on those windows requires sharp reflexes, something that naturally diminishes with age. Warren admitted the bout will look different than it would have years ago, predicting a tighter, less mobile collision where neither heavyweight retreats.

“I think they’ll both be a little bit slower than they were,” Warren said. “I think it’ll be very exciting whilst it lasts.”

Warren dresses it up with complex talk about technical openings and counter angles, but the fundamental flaw is Joshua’s punch resistance. Once a heavyweight’s chin cracks, no amount of technical adjustment can compensate for it.

The warning signs were impossible to miss against Kristian Prenga. Surviving Dubois is one thing because Daniel hits with concussive force, but getting buzzed and nearly closed out by a fringe guy like Prenga signals that Joshua’s internal alarm system is permanently compromised. Every time clean contact lands, his legs betray him immediately.

Fury does not possess one-punch power, yet that makes little difference when the target crumples under ordinary pressure. With his towering frame and natural bulk, Fury merely needs to absorb the initial storm, step into the pocket, and let his hands go until something connects flush. A clean tap on a ruined chin does the exact same job as an explosive shot.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Aims To Become Undisputed Champion
Sports.content:
Las Vegas, Nevada – On Saturday night, Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) defended his WBC junior middleweight championship at The Chelsea inside the Cosmopolitan Casino against the very tough and gritty Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs).

It was a much more challenging match than many expected; Hadribeaj tested Fundora on the inside by making him miss and countering him with an efficient attack. The Albanian Sniper’s total connect rate of 32.3 percent was more effective than The Towering Inferno’s 25.9

percent.

However, Sebastian did outland Ermal in total punches 202 to 144, outlanding him8 of the 12 rounds(Compubox). Fundora was able to score the finishing blow in the last second of the twelve-round fight, winning the fight by controversial knockout.

After the fight, Sebastian said, “It was an interesting fight. I had to go back and fight on the inside and show everyone again that I can still do that. It was dramatic to knock him out at the last second, but we’ll go back to the gym and fix some things.”

He added whom he’ll like to fight next by saying, “I want to go for undisputed in this division. We’ll break either Jaron Ennis or Josh Kelly down just like the last guy and the guy before that. We’ll keep breaking them down. When asked of the two whom he expects to win, Fundora answered, “I do favor Boots.” Meaning him and promoter Sampson Lewkowicz believe it will be Boots whom they’ll have to negotiate for the undisputed crown, but they appear they’ll be playing hardball in negotiations.

Lewkowicz told the media after the fight what he expects the terms of the contract to be, “It doesn’t make any difference…because we need each other. We need 50-50 because we want to unify. It doesn’t matter how many titles. I see so many st**d guys saying on the internet saying he has three belts. You have only two. People already saying he has three.

So many people saying he have three belts. Who’s he fighting? A bum? I respect boxing, and I tell you Kelly can fight.” Sampson went on to state he had already spoken to Jaron’s advisor on the expectations of terms, making it known it should be a 50-50 fight, and hopes they don’t deviate from it by requesting a higher percentage for themselves.

However, if the fight for undisputed does happen next year, the winner of the Boots-Kelly fight will be a three-belt holder bringing the WBA, WBO, and IBF titles to the table, with Fundora holding the single WBC belt. The undisputed showdown is a fight fans will want to see and will truly crown the junior middleweight king.

Hopefully both sides can come to an amicable agreement, and the fight won’t get derailed as were the contract negotiations between Boots and Vergil Ortiz Jr. For now, Sebastian will rest and wait for the Boots-Kelly winner and prepare for his next goal of becoming undisputed junior middleweight king.

Ghana News.title: A case for a systematic rollout of Ghana’s new traffic law (L.I. 2519
Ghana News.content:
Barima Acheampong Sarpong II (Asante Asamanghene)

The Government of Ghana recently announced the rollout of a new set of road traffic regulations, aiming to curb the spate of road accidents in the country.

Like any other efforts by previous administrations which sought to deal with the carnage on our roads, the new regulations could, by intent, be a positive move. The law must, however be rolled out systematically and implemented thoughtfully, else it is bound to fail.

The regulations in question, ‘Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519)’, stand to fail if the government enforces all penalties simultaneously. The law, as has been put out, covers dozens of offences, from speeding to preaching in moving vehicles, with penalties that have jumped dramatically from what pertained in the old regulations. Three structural barriers make a “big bang” approach unworkable: Drivers are largely uninformed about the new rules, enforcement infrastructure is not ready, and compliance costs are stacking up.

The government must adopt a phased, systematic rollout that prioritizes fatal offences, builds infrastructure first, and educates the general public, and those the new rules affect directly in particular, before it penalizes offenders.

Changes in the new L.I from the old law appear drastic. This amounts to a sweeping overhaul. The law covers offences ranging from street racing, jumping red lights, and failing to stop at STOP signs to parking in disabled designated spaces and unauthorised use of bus stops. Preaching or hawking in a moving commercial vehicle now also carries a jail term of three to eight months, up from the previous maximum of 30 days, while fines range from 5 penalty units to 200 penalty units, with one penalty unit valued at GH¢12 .

What makes a law like this problematic is that, when you put these many behaviours together and criminalise them at once, you create a situation where a large portion of drivers are technically in violation of something. That undermines the moral authority of the law and makes selective enforcement inevitable.

One key concern regarding the coming of this new road traffic law is that there has not been adequate public and stakeholder engagement. The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) has stated that its members were not consulted before the L.I was passed, and remain unaware of the new rules. How can drivers comply with a law they do not understand?

The Ministry of Transport launched a nationwide education exercise in September 2026, with Transport Minister Joseph Bukari Nikpe acknowledging that nationwide education was “necessary to help drivers, transport operators, motor unions and other road users understand their responsibilities”. But one month of sensitization is certainly not enough time to absorb dozens of new offences and changed penalties.

As the GPRTU has argued, drivers need to be properly educated before enforcement begins. Penalizing people for violations they did not know existed is not enforcement—it is ambush.

It is a fact and legitimate argument to make also that the government has not put in place the needed infrastructure that will cater for effective implementation of the new law. CUTS International, a policy think tank, has publicly called on the government to delay full enforcement until traffic lights and road markings at enforcement locations have been inspected and repaired.

Their concerns are specific: some traffic lights across Accra are obscured by overgrown trees, others are damaged or out of service. At some junctions, one of two traffic lights works while the other does not. Faded lane markings and stop lines make it impossible for drivers to know where they should stop.

CUTS further put it bluntly: “The purpose of TRAFFITECH-GH is safer roads, not tickets arising from traffic lights drivers could not see”

And, it is worth noting that the government itself has acknowledged the need for more preparation. The Ghana Police Service rescheduled the full implementation of TRAFFITECH-GH from October 1 to November 1, specifically to allow for “more extensive public awareness and education.” This postponement is tacit recognition that the original timeline was too aggressive.

The compliance cost of new driver’s licence presents yet another element of challenge. The GPRTU has warned that the new licensing requirements could leave commercial drivers paying for up to three different licences—a professional driver’s licence, a separate commercial driver’s licence, and existing MMDA permits. The union’s deputy PRO pointed out: “It will not help businesses because if it happens like that, then it means we will be paying too much, increasing our operational cost”.

The mandatory towing requirement adds another layer of cost. Vehicle owners must now subscribe to a towing service or hold an insurance policy with towing cover. The previous 30-minute to one-hour grace period has been eliminated entirely—vehicles must be towed immediately upon breakdown. After 21 days, vehicles can be auctioned.

The GPRTU opposes the auction provision, arguing that “nobody will intentionally leave his vehicle on the road”, and that owners should be allowed to reclaim vehicles after paying towing and storage fees. What happens in this circumstance is that when compliance costs rise sharply while enforcement expands simultaneously, drivers face a rational calculation: the cost of obeying may exceed the cost of violating. That is not a recipe for compliance.

Statistically, the data on Ghana’s road accident deaths suggests the need for prioritization. Ghana recorded 2,949 road deaths in 2025, the highest in 35 years and an 18.2% increase over 2024. Speeding accounted for more than 60% of all collisions. Motorcycle crashes rose by 19.4%, with 6,548 motorcycles involved in crashes.

If the government focuses enforcement resources on these killers—speeding, drunk driving, red-light running, motorcycle helmet use—the safety gains will be immediate and measurable. Spreading limited enforcement capacity across preaching, hawking, parking violations, and administrative offences dilutes the impact on what actually kills people. The police have already indicated that the initial phase of TRAFFITECH-GH will focus on speeding. This is the right instinct. It should be formalized into policy.

To ensure effective implementation of the new road traffic regulations, enforce should focus strictly on offences with the clearest link to fatalities: speeding, red-light running, drunk driving, motorcycle helmet use, and seat belt use. These have the strongest public consensus and the highest safety return.



An equally important measure is to include offences that require physical infrastructure to comply with, such as stopping at YIELD signs, pedestrian crossing rules, bus stop regulations. Here, the relevant infrastructure should be provided before enforcement. Where such infrastructure exists, it should be functional.

The introduction of administrative and nuisance offences should come last. By that point drivers would have experienced a functioning system for about a year and understand the expectations.

It is expected for some to argue that gradualism signals weakness—that the government is not serious, that indiscipline continues while authorities tiptoe. The 2,949 deaths demand urgency.

But urgency does not require chaos. The government can signal seriousness by strictly enforcing a focused set of critical offences while phasing in the rest. Here the message becomes: “We are serious about saving lives, and we are doing this properly.” That is more credible than a blitz that collapses under its own weight, breeds corruption, and alienates the very drivers whose cooperation is essential.

In all, L.I. 2519 contains the right intentions. But good intentions do not make good policy. A law that overwhelms the enforcement system, punishes drivers for infrastructure failures, and imposes costs that make compliance irrational will not save lives. It will generate resentment, bribery, and evasion.

A systematic, phased approach—prioritizing fatal offences, building infrastructure first, and educating before penalizing—gives the law a chance to work. The goal is not to punish the maximum number of people. The goal is to reduce the 2,949 deaths. That requires strategy, not shock therapy.

Before issuing any fine, there should be complete visibility inspections at every enforcement location. Repair obscured signals, repaint faded markings, install missing speed limit signs. There should be face-to-face education with commercial driver unions. Equally, there should be verification to ensure that the vehicles registration database can accurately identify offenders.

Ghana News.title: Sam George outlines $270m Ghana AI investment, cites risks of feeding government data into foreign models
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has outlined a $270 million investment in Ghana’s artificial intelligence (AI) development, with $250 million earmarked for infrastructure and computing capacity and the remaining $20 million for seed funding for an AI fund.

He said the investment would support the development of Ghana’s AI infrastructure, including a national language-processing model, amid concerns about sensitive government information being fed into foreign AI platforms.

Speaking during JoyNews' Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on Wednesday, October 21, Mr George said he had observed instances where classified government material was being entered into platforms such as ChatGPT and Claude by analysts working in ministers’ offices.

“That for me represents a critical national risk because memos, government material, critical government sensitive data is being fed into these systems by analysts sitting in ministers' offices to process that data,” he said.

He questioned the effectiveness of the country’s data residency law if government institutions continued to rely on foreign AI models to process sensitive information.

“Now we have a residency law that we've passed, but it's useless if the government system itself is using a foreign AI model to do processing,” he said.

Mr George said the government was working towards developing what he called the “Ghana Chat”, a national language-processing model that would allow government institutions to use AI while building local capacity.

He said the initiative was also intended to ensure that the public sector benefited from the speed and computing power of AI without compromising sensitive government data.

The Minister acknowledged that the proposed model would not initially match the capabilities of established platforms such as ChatGPT and Claude but said its performance would improve through continued use and training.

“At start, will it be as effective as Claude and ChatGPT? Definitely not. But then the more you use it and the more you teach it, the more the machines learn, the better the system will get,” he said.

He added that existing AI systems had been built, piloted and trained using billions, if not trillions, of data points, suggesting that Ghana’s model would similarly require time and training to improve.

Mr George acknowledged the questions and concerns raised about the initiative but expressed confidence that the proposed approach would help address the issues.

“So basically I see all the questions that are being raised, very legitimate questions, very legitimate issues, but I believe that we are on the right track to resolving all of those issues,” he said.

Ghana News.title: ‘Those who evolve and adapt will survive’ – Sam George on AI and jobs
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, says that workers who fail to adapt to changing technology risk losing their jobs as artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes the world of work.

According to him, the ability to evolve and acquire new skills will be critical for workers seeking to remain relevant as workplaces increasingly adopt new technologies.

Speaking during the Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on JoyNews on Wednesday, October 21, Mr George said technological advancement had historically transformed jobs, forcing workers to learn new skills to remain employable.

“Those who evolve and adapt will survive. Those who fail to evolve and adapt will fall off. It's the hard reality of artificial intelligence,” he said.

To illustrate his point, the Minister recounted the experience of an aunt who worked as a Grade Three stenographer in the public service when he was younger.

He explained that she used a manual typewriter before the introduction of electronic typewriters and computers gradually changed how office work was performed.

According to him, workers who relied on traditional typewriters had to learn how to use computers and software applications, including Microsoft Office, as workplaces modernised.

Mr George said his aunt would have risked losing her job if she had failed to acquire the skills needed to operate the new technology.

“If she did not learn with Mavis Beacon, as most people did at that time, how to use the Microsoft Office suite, she would have lost her job because by 2000 you didn't have any typewriters sitting in the public service,” he said.

He used the example to underscore the importance of continuous learning and adaptation as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into professional and business activities.

The Minister’s remarks highlight the growing debate over AI’s implications for employment, with workers and businesses facing pressure to develop new capabilities as technology changes how tasks are performed.

He added that, as with previous technological shifts, the ability to adapt will be essential for workers navigating the changes artificial intelligence brings to the workplace.

Ghana News.title: African mineral value addition in focus at ‘Mining in Motion Conference’
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF), Justina Nelson, has highlighted the importance of investment, data sharing and regional cooperation in helping African countries derive greater value from their mineral resources.

She made the remarks during a ministerial roundtable on mineral value addition and beneficiation at the African Minerals Policy Forum (Mining in Motion Conference) in Accra on October 19, 2026.

The session, held at the Destiny Arena in Haatso, brought together representatives of African governments, continental institutions and international development organisations to explore strategies for moving beyond the export of raw minerals towards local processing and manufacturing.

Mrs Nelson highlighted the opportunities presented by government policies aimed at attracting investment and promoting value addition across the mining value chain.

She noted that these efforts could support job creation, strengthen local industries and increase the economic benefits African countries derive from their mineral resources.

She also emphasised the importance of sharing geological and other relevant data to improve understanding of Africa’s critical mineral resources and identify opportunities for their effective utilisation.

Regional integration and cooperation, she noted, are important to strengthening mineral value chains and enabling African countries to benefit more from their collective resource wealth.

Participants at the roundtable identified reliable and affordable energy, access to finance, transport infrastructure, geological data and technical skills as key requirements for developing viable mineral processing industries.

They also highlighted the importance of effective regulatory frameworks and stronger coordination among governments, investors and development institutions. Participants also considered the potential to process minerals used in clean energy technologies, including lithium, into higher-value products.

Mrs Nelson emphasised the need to translate existing policies and legislation into practical outcomes, noting that commitments to beneficiation must be matched by effective implementation and tangible investment. She also underscored the importance of managing Africa’s mineral resources in ways that deliver lasting benefits for present and future generations.

The roundtable formed part of the African Minerals Policy Forum, known as the Mining in Motion Conference (AMPF-MiM), a platform focused on advancing the African Mining Vision. Adopted by African Heads of State, the vision seeks to harness Africa’s mineral resources to promote inclusive economic growth, industrialization and sustainable development.

The discussions highlighted the importance of investment, effective policies and regional collaboration in strengthening Africa’s capacity to process its mineral resources locally and retain a greater share of the economic value generated by the mining sector.

Ghana News.title: Black Maidens fight back to hold Brazil in six-goal thriller
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s Black Maidens mounted a determined fightback to hold Brazil to a pulsating 3-3 draw on Wednesday night, with Priscilla Mensah striking five minutes from time to deny the South Americans victory at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

In a six-goal encounter, Ghana showed resilience against one of the tournament favourites, recovering from an early setback and responding again after Brazil had twice regained the lead.

The result gives the Black Maidens their first point of the campaign after two matches, keeping alive their hopes of progressing to the knockout stage.

Brazil made the brighter start and needed only seven minutes to break the deadlock, with Nicolly finding the net to put Ghana under early pressure.

Rather than retreat, the Maidens gradually worked their way back into the contest and were rewarded in the 31st minute when Rafia Osman restored parity.

Ghana then seized the initiative. Four minutes after the equaliser, Gloria Ameaa struck to put the West Africans 2-1 ahead and raise hopes of a significant result against the highly rated Brazilians.

But the advantage proved short-lived. Kaillany Rafinah scored in the 44th minute to bring Brazil level at 2-2 just before the interval, leaving the contest finely poised at half-time.

Brazil resumed with greater purpose and regained the lead in the 57th minute through Indy, forcing Ghana to chase the game once more.

The Maidens pressed for another equaliser as the clock ticked down, refusing to let the deficit end their hopes of taking something from the encounter.

Their persistence paid off in the 85th minute when Mensah found the back of the net to make it 3-3 and rescue a valuable point for Ghana.

The draw leaves Ghana with one point from two matches and at the bottom of Group C, but their qualification hopes remain alive ahead of their final group fixture.

The Black Maidens must now turn their attention to Canada, with the encounter set to be crucial to their chances of reaching the next round.

Ghana News.title: Sam George announces national data exchange hub to connect 48 public registries
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has announced plans to establish a national data exchange hub to connect 48 public data registries and enable seamless information sharing across government institutions.

According to him, the initiative is expected to eliminate the need for developers and businesses to establish separate connections with individual public institutions to access data, while improving data classification and interoperability across the country.

Speaking during the Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on JoyNews on Wednesday, October 21, Mr George said the proposed hub would provide a single national backbone through which public data registries could exchange information.

“We have about 48 data registries in the country that process from the Ghana Health Service to the National Identification Authority to the Ghana Statistical Service. Literally any data set in the country is processed by one data processor that doesn't speak to the other,” he said.

He explained that the current arrangement required entities seeking information from multiple institutions to establish separate connections with each registry.

Using Hubtel as an example, the Minister said a request for data could require the company to establish connections with all 48 registries.

He, however, noted that under the proposed system, developers would be able to submit a single request through the exchange hub to access data from multiple institutions, including the National Identification Authority, Ghana Statistical Service, Births and Deaths Registry and Ghana Police Service.

“What we're doing is we're building a single national backbone where all our 48 public registries connect seamlessly in an interoperable manner to that backbone,” he said.

Mr George said the National Information Technology Agency (NITA) would introduce standards to ensure that data processors classify and organise information uniformly across the country.

He said the approach would help address inconsistencies in data classification and annotation through a unified policy framework.

The Minister stressed that the initiative would not require public institutions to surrender ownership or control of their databases.

“Now all data processors are still going to hold their data and be responsible for their data, but all you do is you have a single point where you query that data as a developer,” he explained.

Mr George said the initial phase would focus on public data registries, with plans to create opportunities for private sector participation.

Although private companies would not be compelled to join the system, he said access to government-controlled data would be linked to their contribution to the exchange ecosystem.

“So if you're a private sector player and you also hold data and you want the data that government is controlling, you need to contribute your data so that you're part of the ecosystem,” he said.

The Minister said that the proposed data exchange hub forms part of efforts to improve data interoperability and create a more connected digital ecosystem in Ghana, with potential applications for businesses, public service delivery and the development of artificial intelligence solutions.

Ghana News.title: Bleoo ’15 launches ‘Adopt a Classroom’ project to improve learning environment at Accra Academy
Ghana News.content:
2015 Year Group of Accra Academy

The 2015 Year Group of Accra Academy, popularly known as Bleoo ’15, has launched its signature ‘Adopt a Classroom’ project, an initiative aimed at renovating and modernising classrooms at the school to create a better learning environment for current and future students.

The project was announced at a ceremony at the K.G. Konuah Hall of Accra Academy, where Bleoo ’15 was formally inaugurated, marking a new chapter in the year group’s commitment to alumni welfare, school development and service to its alma mater.

The ‘Adopt a Classroom’ initiative seeks to mobilise support from old boys, corporate organisations and well-meaning individuals to improve classroom facilities and contribute to the school’s continued pursuit of academic excellence.

Speaking at the event, Bleoo ’15 President, Manuel Koranteng, called on members to look beyond individual achievements and work together to build a united, organised and supportive year group committed to making a lasting impact.

Bleoo ’15 President, Manuel Koranteng

He also announced a GHS 10,000 seed for the establishment of Bleoo ’15 Cares Fund, which will provide support to members experiencing bereavement, medical emergencies and other personal hardships.

Drawing on Accra Academy’s motto, Esse Quam Videri — “To be, rather than to seem” — Mr Koranteng urged members to translate their pride in the school into tangible contributions that would improve the experiences of students and strengthen the institution for generations to come.

The inauguration ceremony brought together alumni, school authorities, representatives of other year groups, members of the SMOGA 2015 Year Group and students from invited schools.

Guest speaker Stephen Antah of Bleoo ’99, alongside Kofi Amoa-Awuah, President of the Accra Academy Old Boys Association (AAOBA), and the President of SMOGA ’15, offered words of encouragement to the newly inaugurated year group.

With the launch of the ‘Adopt a Classroom’ project and the formal inauguration of the year group, Bleoo ’15 has set out an agenda that combines member welfare with a commitment to educational development.

The year group is calling on alumni, corporate organisations and individuals to support the initiative and help turn its vision into reality. For Bleoo ’15, its legacy will be measured not simply by the milestones it celebrates, but by the opportunities it helps create for the next generation of Accra Academy students.

Ghana News.title: KNUST, MTN sign MoU to strengthen industry-academia collaboration and develop AI talent
Ghana News.content:
Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with telecommunications company MTN Ghana to strengthen industry-academia collaboration, equip students with practical skills and develop homegrown solutions to Ghana’s technological challenges.

The partnership is expected to create opportunities for student internships, graduate recruitment, industry-led training and the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to real-world problems.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, MTN’s Senior Manager for Digital Analytics and Monetization, Kwame Adu Manu, said the partnership would help bridge the gap between academic training and industry requirements while enabling talented graduates to contribute to national development.

“We want to bridge that gap between industry and academia, and this is one of the excellent ways to do that,” he said.

He explained that MTN would provide students with hands-on experience through practical projects, allowing them to apply the knowledge acquired in the classroom to challenges within the telecommunications industry.

According to him, the initiative would also help address brain drain by encouraging highly skilled graduates to remain in Ghana and contribute to the country’s development.

“We want to change that status quo, bring them to MTN, give them hands-on projects, and then they get to have an impact on Ghana and their society,” he noted.

Mr Adu Manu further highlighted the importance of developing AI solutions that respond to the needs of African communities, arguing that greater local participation in AI development was necessary to address problems unique to the continent.

He said MTN intended to use the partnership to give students opportunities to work on practical AI projects through the company’s Digital Analytics and Monetization department.

“We want to build solutions for Africa, for ourselves, for Ghana to solve our own problems,” he added.

As part of the collaboration, MTN officials are also expected to deliver guest lectures and engage students directly to expose them to industry practices and career opportunities.

The Vice-Chancellor of KNUST, Professor Christian Agyare, described the agreement as evidence of the university’s commitment to building stronger relationships with industry to improve teaching, research and innovation.

He said the collaboration would enable the university’s faculty and students to work with MTN to develop solutions to challenges facing the company and other stakeholders.

Professor Agyare disclosed that MTN would award scholarships to the three best graduating Computer Science students, as well as an additional scholarship to the best graduating female student.

He said the support for the best graduating female student was particularly important in encouraging more women to pursue programmes in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM).

“KNUST faculty members would have opportunities to contribute their expertise and competencies towards addressing challenges identified by MTN,” he said

Professor Agyare said the agreement would incorporate a monitoring, evaluation and learning framework to assess progress, identify implementation gaps and improve the partnership over time.

He explained that the university’s Department of Computer Science would help oversee the implementation of the MoU, working alongside MTN to ensure the collaboration delivers its intended outcomes.

He expressed optimism that the collaboration between the two institutions would extend beyond the immediate commitments and produce benefits for the university, MTN and Ghana as a whole.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Man United captain Fernandes slams Carrick’s tactics after Como hammering
World.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno ‌Fernandes said his side failed to apply enough pressure and adopted ⁠a “mood of defeat” ⁠after conceding early in Wednesday’s 4–1 Champions League loss at Como, a result that increased scrutiny on manager Michael Carrick.

Como opened the scoring ⁠in the second minute, and United collapsed, with only a stoppage-time consolation goal from Joshua Zirkzee making the scoreline slightly less severe.

“We started on the wrong ⁠foot, and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “There was not enough pressure on the ball and not many good movements off the ball. There were many things not going our way.

“It’s a decision from the [coaching] staff not to press man-to-man ‌and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said.

Asked if his comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me.

“Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and ⁠making them uncomfortable.”

Carrick has come under increasing pressure with ⁠United now winless in seven matches.

“It was more than disappointing,” the 45-year-old manager told TNT Sports. “I think everybody’s got to take responsibility for that. I’ll take responsibility for the overall team and performance; it stops with me, and I’m fine with that.

“But as a supporter of this football club, to see a ⁠performance like that is unacceptable, I have to ⁠say.”



Carrick said his side had failed to show the required intensity.

“It’s the motivation and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football that you have to bring. We didn’t bring that today,” ‌he said. “I’ve got to apologise for the performance.”

Fernandes also questioned United’s mentality after the early setback.

“Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood ‌of ‌defeat,” he said.

United have three points from their opening three Champions League matches and host AS Roma in their next fixture in the competition.
