World.title: Iraq plans to purchase 10 large oil tankers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is moving toward the acquisition of supertankers to bolster its capacity for transporting and marketing crude oil globally—a strategic step intended to reduce transportation costs and enhance financial returns from crude exports.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is considering the purchase of 10 oil tankers as part of its efforts to develop its export infrastructure and expand options for delivering shipments to global markets.

The step is part of the government’s efforts to strengthen the role of the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC) and leverage the ownership of maritime transport assets, which would provide greater flexibility in marketing crude oil and managing shipments.

The plan is considered crucial given Iraq’s desire to improve the terms of its oil sales and reduce the discounts associated with certain existing marketing and transportation arrangements.

In a televised statement, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair revealed that the ministry is considering the purchase of 10 supertankers, with an estimated total cost of $2 billion, according to Attaqa News.

According to Khudair, the projected fleet will have a total capacity of 10 million barrels since each tanker has a capacity of around one million barrels.

Owning these tankers would increase export earnings; estimates indicate that Iraq might save between 30 percent and 40 percent on the losses it presently suffers from price reductions.

The Ministry of Oil has more alternatives than only direct procurement; it is also considering proposals from specialist companies to establish joint ventures for the supply of oil tankers.

According to Khudair, one of the suggestions is specialized businesses funding the acquisition of tankers in exchange for a portion of the revenues made from the vessels’ operations, with the price paid over a period of three or four years.

Direct procurement is still a possibility, and the Iraqi government has said that it supports this approach.

World.title: Iraq’s Diwaniyah refinery undergoes major $800 million expansion project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An oil refinery expansion project in Iraq is making tangible progress, as part of the country’s efforts to reduce its reliance on imported fuel and increase the value of its crude oil.

The Al-Barham Group (ABG) is carrying out an $800 million expansion project at the Diwaniyah refinery in Iraq.

This project is one of several refinery expansion initiatives that Iraq is pursuing, including those in al-Amarah, Muthanna, Kirkuk, and Qayyarah.

The refinery manager projected in September 2025 that monthly revenues would reach approximately $35 million once the expansion is complete.

The Diwaniyah refinery expansion is progressing steadily toward the operational phase. An atmospheric distillation unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day will bring the refinery’s total production capacity to 90,000 barrels per day—more than four times its current capacity—according to the British magazine Middle East Economic Digest (MEED).

The Iraqi government signed the expansion deal in February 2025. The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) declared that the contractor will start moving equipment on-site within days after securing the required finance.

In July 2025, work officially commenced at the site, with the Ministry of Oil establishing a five-year timeline for the project’s completion.

In addition to the main distillation unit, the project includes a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) processing unit with a capacity of 180 tons per day, a naphtha hydro-treating unit with a capacity of 18,000 barrels per day, a gasoline upgrading unit with a capacity of 10,000 barrels per day, a naphtha isomerization unit with a capacity of 8,000 barrels per day, and a loading terminal with a capacity of 90,000 barrels per day.

The project also includes a power generation plant, a nitrogen plant, a water pumping and purification station, an industrial wastewater treatment plant, and 24 storage tanks for crude oil and petroleum products.

Beside high-quality gasoline, the refinery will produce naphtha, kerosene, red diesel, fuel oil, and LPG, supporting Iraq’s objective of achieving self-sufficiency in petroleum products.

World.title: Iraq’s customs revenues hit record high in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s General Authority of Customs has announced a revenue increase of over $72 million in September 2026 compared to the same month in 2025.

The authority said in a statement that total customs revenues rose from $222.8 million in September 2025 to $294.8 million in September 2026—a growth rate of approximately 32.34 percent.

The rise reflects the importance of developing the customs operational system and enhancing the efficiency of revenue collection in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The authority indicated that it is implementing a plan to enhance institutional performance, improve customs operational procedures, and increase the efficiency of revenue collection.

The measures are designed to protect public funds, strengthen the state’s financial resources, support financial reform, and promote the growth of non-oil revenues.

In January, head of the authority’s valuation department, Ahmed al-Akeedi, said that the deployment of the ASYCUDA system and the new customs tariff will improve earnings.

Al-Akeedi said that Iraqi customs revenues reached $1.9 billion in 2025, an unprecedented milestone in Iraqi customs history and an exceptional achievement.

Revenues are predicted to grow by at least four to six times with the application of the ASYCUDA system and complete compliance with customs rates, perhaps exceeding $7.63 billion by the end of 2026, according to al-Akeedi.

World.title: Iraq shuts Sheeb border crossing with Iran for security reasons
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has closed the al-Sheeb border crossing with Iran to all passengers, vehicles, and commercial transit until further notice.

An Iraqi border crossings official told Reuters that the sudden shutdown on Wednesday was implemented to review existing security procedures and install advanced detection equipment.

Officials mentioned that current security protocols at the busy Maysan province crossing were weak and inadequate to effectively halt the smuggling of prohibited materials.

Iranian security official Valiollah Hayati has advised passengers and cargo trucks to divert to the Shalamcheh crossing in Khuzestan province.

No official date has been announced for the resumption of operations. Local reports suggest the Iraqi government is currently evaluating security at other checkpoints and may gradually close additional borders with Iran in the coming days.

Iran’s Interior Ministry is currently in talks with Iraqi provincial authorities to coordinate a timeline for reopening the border.

In mid-September, Iraq announced the resumption of trade through its border crossings with Iran, following a brief closure due to security concerns.

Iraq closed several border crossings with Iran following a drone attack targeting a pipeline in Saudi Arabia, which Riyadh and Baghdad said originated from Iraqi territory.

Iraqi authorities had discovered drone launchers near the Iraqi-Iranian border in the remote al-Tayeb area in the ​​southern province of Maysan.

World.title: Five things to know about Chinese AI startup DeepSeek
World.content:
Beijing – The United States Department of Homeland Security ordered government agencies on Monday to stop using artificial intelligence tools from DeepSeek, citing concerns over data being transferred to China.

Here are five things to know about the Chinese AI startup following the new restrictions:

– ‘Sputnik moment’ –

Founded by Liang Wenfeng in the eastern Chinese tech hub Hangzhou, DeepSeek started life in 2023 as a side project of Liang’s data-driven hedge fund that had access to a cache of powerful AI processors made by US chip giant Nvidia.

It gained global attention in January 2025 with the release of its R1 deep-reasoning large language model, which sparked a US tech share sell-off.

Industry insiders were stunned by R1’s high performance — at a level similar to ChatGPT and other leading US chatbots — and DeepSeek’s claims to have developed it at a fraction of the cost.

Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen described it as a “Sputnik moment”, referencing the 1957 launch of Earth’s first artificial satellite by the Soviet Union that stunned the Western world.

– Censorship concerns –

Like other Chinese chatbots, DeepSeek’s AI tools eschew topics usually censored in the world’s second-largest economy, such as the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown.

That and data privacy concerns have led DeepSeek AI to be banned or restricted on government-issued devices in several countries, including the United States, Australia and South Korea.

On Monday, the US went further by banning civilian government agencies from using products developed by DeepSeek and third-party tools created using DeepSeek.

China’s foreign ministry said it opposed that move and accused the US of “overstretching” the concept of national security.

DeepSeek’s low cost and ease of deployment have made it a popular choice in developing countries, analysts say.

The company holds around four percent of global market share for chatbots, according to web traffic analysis company Similarweb. ChatGPT dominates at 68 percent.

– Open source –

DeepSeek’s systems are open-source, meaning their inner workings are public, allowing programmers to customise parts of the software to suit their needs.

That is the same for other major Chinese AI players, including tech giant Alibaba, in contrast to the “closed” models sold by OpenAI and other Western rivals.

The Chinese government has trumpeted its lead in open-source AI technology, which it says can accelerate innovation.

“Chinese AI models are leading the way in the open-source innovation ecosystem,” National People’s Congress spokesman Lou Qinjian told policymakers in April.

– Startup boost –

The success of DeepSeek has galvanised China’s AI scene, despite hurdles posed by rivalry with the United States and fears of a global market bubble.

Shares in two leading Chinese AI startups, Zhipu AI and MiniMax, soared on their market debuts in Hong Kong this year, and it has been a similar story for Chinese chipmakers such as MetaX.

In June, investors valued DeepSeek at more than $50 billion in the company’s first funding round, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Shi Yaqiong and her team at Beijing-based Jinqiu Capital told AFP there has been a “clear surge” in enthusiasm around Chinese AI — and competition among investors — since the DeepSeek shock.

– Chip smuggling reports –

DeepSeek’s rise has not been without controversy.

Reports, including in technology outlet The Information, say DeepSeek has been skirting a US ban on the export of top-end chips to China to train its new V4 model.

The Information said in December, citing six people with knowledge of the matter, that DeepSeek developed V4 using thousands of chips dismantled in third countries and smuggled to China.

DeepSeek did not respond to AFP’s request for comment at the time. Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment but told The Information that they had not seen any evidence of this and that “such smuggling seems farfetched”.

In April, DeepSeek said it had used both Nvidia and Huawei’s domestically-produced Ascend chips for its new model.

Huawei, at the forefront of Chinese efforts to reduce reliance on US semiconductor technology, said in a statement that the full range of its Ascend products support DeepSeek’s V4 series.

Washington says DeepSeek’s latest model is about eight months behind the top offerings from US companies.

World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves rise to $81.5 billion in August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed on Wednesday that the country’s foreign reserves rose to $81.53 billion by the end of August 2026, compared to $80.633 billion at the end of July.

Iraq’s foreign reserves increased by approximately $905 million during August but remained below the level recorded at the end of 2025, when they stood at $97.43 billion. Throughout the first eight months of this year, there has been a $15.89 billion decrease.

After reaching $101.08 billion at the end of January 2026, Iraq’s foreign reserves fell to $100.34 billion in March, $97.8 billion in April, $93.67 billion in May, $86.17 billion in June, and $80.63 billion in July before rising once again in August.

Last month, the CBI confirmed that its foreign currency reserves are entirely sufficient to meet all market demands.

Earlier in October, a Standard Chartered economist said that Iraq may resort to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) if oil revenues continue to fall and the currency’s devaluation fails to boost state finances as intended.

Standard Chartered chief economist for the Middle East and Pakistan Carla Slim said that any potential program with the IMF could entail structural reforms, particularly regarding the public sector wage bill, to enhance fiscal sustainability, Bloomberg reported.

If the current pace of depletion continues, Iraq’s foreign reserves might fall to roughly $60 billion by the end of the year, down from over $100 billion at the beginning of the year, according to Slim.

World.title: France’s tourism sector worried about impact of riots
World.content:
Paris – The images of France’s riots posted and broadcast around the world have cast a pall on the country’s important tourism sector, with many fearing worse consequences if violence returns.

“The surge of violence in the centres of Nice, Paris, Lyon — it’s catastrophic,” said Christelle Cassagne, head of the ADN Tourisme body covering the country’s tourism institutions.

“When you book a hotel for a week, it’s not so you stay stuck in the hotel,” she said.

The scenes of clashes with police, public buildings on fire, shops being looted and masked young men roaming the streets have, since last weekend, shocked and fascinated news audiences internationally.

The violence has usurped the usual curated footage of genteel cafes favoured by influencers, who have suddenly taken to asking “Is Paris safe?” — many using AI on thumbnails or even in their videos to boost click-through rates.

Even in Paris, some tourists who had front-row seats to the convulsion on the streets are looking for the exit. And others coming in were hesitant.

“Honestly, we were not certain that we’d keep our stay,” an Indian businessman in a pricey Paris hotel said, declining to give his name.

Already, hotel reservations are weakening in major cities such as Paris, Lyon and Marseille, according to Didier Arino, head of the consulting and research firm Protourisme.

For a country used to welcoming 100 million visitors a year — and the more than 70 billion euros ($80 billion) they spend — it’s a concern.

Arino and other observers questioned by AFP said the overall picture for France’s tourism industry would depend on whether new violence broke out in the coming weeks.

“The impact of a day of rioting and urban violence in the heart of Paris caused around a one-percent cancellation rate for the monthly count in the days following, and the same for the following weeks,” Arino said.

“For the 42 million hotel nights forecast for 2026, that’s not major. But watch out you don’t underestimate the effects from repeated incidents.”

That could also flow through to tourism revenues, as visitors from those countries often have more spending power than Europeans.

– Travel advisories –

The downward pressure on reservations comes as several countries, including the United States, China and Germany issued travel advisories for their citizens in France.

“The further away the clients are, the more sensitive they are to safety risks, and the stronger the impact,” said Arino.

Laurent Abitbol, head of the executive board of travel agency group Selectour, said: “If this lasts two weeks, that’s not so serious. However, if this continues for several months it will be catastrophic.”

“When you watch CNN, or Fox News, BBC, all that, you’d believe that France is at war. That’s not good…”

Another firm, MKG Consulting, said that, since last weekend, Paris hotels have lost potential bookings for the next six weeks.

Its data showed bookings had weakened sharply within a day.

Between October 19 and 20, the share of rooms booked for stays from October 20-29 fell from being 1.0 percentage point above the level recorded for the same period in 2025 to just 0.2 percentage points higher.

For stays between October 20 and 25, the increase over 2025 levels also narrowed significantly, dropping from 3.5 percentage points to 1.9 points.

“This slowdown is especially notable for near-term and high-end stays,” it said, drawing a parallel with a period in December 2018 when Yellow Vest street protests raged in the capital’s streets.

World.title: Iraq’s domestic public debt climbs to 113.5 trillion dinars in August 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s domestic public debt surged to 113.485 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $86.6 billion) by the end of August 2026, climbing from 109.516 trillion dinars at the end of July.

The monthly increase of 3.969 trillion dinars reflects expanding sovereign borrowing needs to finance fiscal obligations, according to official economic indicators released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI).

Economic data indicates that domestic debt expanded by roughly 22.97 trillion dinars compared to the end of 2025, when it stood at 90.515 trillion dinars.

This represents a steep expansion of 25.4% during the first eight months of 2026, driven by higher reliance on central banking liquidity and domestic sovereign debt instruments to cover budget spending.

The breakdown of domestic obligations at the end of August shows that Ministry of Finance claims held by the Central Bank constituted the primary component, rising to 76.499 trillion dinars from 72.499 trillion dinars in July.

Commercial and sovereign loans represented the second-largest portion at 18.945 trillion dinars, followed by domestic bonds at 9.330 trillion dinars and treasury bills at 8.711 trillion dinars, underlining the structured profile of the central treasury’s internal liabilities.

World.title: Why are uninsured vehicles not part of crash relief scheme? Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With Centre formulating a scheme to provide interim financial relief of Rs 2 lakh to families of road crash victims for deaths and Rs 1 lakh for grievous injuries, limited to accidents involving insured vehicles, SC has sought an explanation from govt on why it is not being extended to uninsured vehicles.

Taking note that âCompensation to Victims (Interim Relief) Scheme, 2026â has not been notified or publicised, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan directed the govt to publicise it to ensure awareness. People must be made aware of their right to seek interim compensation, it said.

Union road transport ministry officials said the scheme will be notified as provided for under Central Motor Vehicle Act.

Govt informed SC that the ministry shared the scheme with states and UTs on Feb 23. SC had directed the ministry in April 2025 to formulate the scheme.

On why it covers only insured vehicles, officials said it was framed under provisions of MV Act dealing with insured vehicles. If the offenderâs vehicle is uninsured, the matter will go to a Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT).

The apex court bench examined clause 6 of the scheme, which specifies that victims or legal heirs of the deceased can apply through a designated online portal, providing details of claims filed or pending before a MACT.





Officials said that Section 164 of the Act, which deals with compensation in cases of death or grievous injury, requires the vehicle owner or insurer to pay Rs 5 lakh and Rs 2.5 lakh for death and serious injury, respectively, under the âno-fault liabilityâ provision. A claimant need not establish that death or injury resulted from wrongful act, neglect or default on the vehicle ownerâs part.

World.title: Rosatom completes supply of engineered safety features actuation systems for Kudankulam N-plant units 3 and 4
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Russia state atomic energy corporation Rosatomâs division Rosatom Automated Control Systems has completed the supply of equipment for engineered safety features actuation system computerised subsystems (ESFAS CS) for units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in Tamil Nadu.

The role of the general designer and supplier of equipment in the project belongs to Atomstroyexport.

In total, about 300 items of equipment were manufactured and delivered to the plant â four sets of ESFAS CS in accordance with the number of safety instrumentation and control trains, per each power unit featuring VVER-1000 reactors.

ESFAS is the system that monitors the process parameters of a power unit when there is a deviation from normal operation conditions.

In case of an accident, the system automatically initiates the start of safety instrumentation and control systems and sends commands to actuators (boron injection pumps and other active protection means) in order to prevent a beyond-design-basis accident and bring the reactor plant to a safe state.

The system also ensures reactor cooldown, which is a controlled decrease of coolant temperature and pressure down to safe values after the shutdown.





To avoid simultaneous failure, they are physically separated â located in different rooms â and have autonomous power supply from separate diesel generators.

Specialists developing the ESFAS CS for units 3 and 4 relied on the operating experience of the same system at Kudankulam NPP units 1 and 2, which allowed them to implement a number of optimised solutions. One of such solutions is the application of non-programmable modules that process signals from sensors without the use of microprocessors.

This helps to reduce the dependence of safety functions on application software and increases the resistance of equipment to potential common cause failures.

The final delivery of ESFAS CS equipment was yet another step of equipping the power units with Russian automation, control and safety systems, implemented through industrial cooperation. Installation on the site will be followed by the pre-commissioning stage, which includes the off-line and integrated tests of the systems.

Following the tests, the systems will be prepared for commissioning and further operation at units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam plant.

Kudankulam plant features six power units with VVER-1000 reactors, with the total installed capacity of 6,000 MW. The first phase (units 1 and 2) was commissioned in 2013 and 2017, respectively. The second phase (Units 3 and 4) is under construction.

World.title: New norms for DL: Driving tutorial pass mark may rise to 75%, select licence services to be free
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Road transport ministry has proposed raising the pass mark for safe-driving tutorial assessment from 60% to 75% and waiving fees for specified driving-licence services availed through online Aadhaar authentication, along with charges for changes to licence particulars such as name and address.

The proposed changes to driving licence rules are aimed at tightening assessment requirements and to ensure availing licence-related services without any hassle. The changes proposed in the draft notification to amend sections of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules published late Wednesday night also seek to streamline online driving licence services, specify acceptable identity and residence documents, and introduce time limits for processing applications to change licence particulars.

Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes. The higher qualifying score of 70% is aimed at making the assessment more stringent. The draft also proposes a defined procedure for online applications to change driving licence particulars, including name and address. Licencing authorities would have to approve or reject applications for changes within 15 days, giving reasons for rejection.





An application for an address change that remains undecided for 30 days would be deemed approved.

The proposed rules also specify documents that can be submitted as proof of identity, age and residence. These include Aadhaar, passport, voter identity card, recognised educational certificates and birth certificates, among other documents. Electricity and household gas bills not older than three months are among the proposed address-proof documents.

LIC policy would no more be accepted as a proof.

The draft also provides for a consolidated application form covering services such as licence renewal, issuance of duplicate licences, addition of a vehicle class and changes to personal particulars. Specified applicant details would be retrieved electronically from the SARATHI portal wherever available.

In another proposed change, a vehicle class would be deleted from a driving licence within seven days of an application to surrender it. However, applicants permanently surrendering a class would not be eligible to obtain a learnerâs or driving licence for that class for one year.

The draft notification invites objections and suggestions from stakeholders within 30 days of publication. The proposals will come into force after final notification.

World.title: Cars to brake on their own: Centre plans AEBS mandate from Oct 2030
World.content:
As for pre-2030 still-in production models, AEBS would mandatory from Oct 2032.

NEW DELHI: Certain safety features of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) will be made mandatory for cars, particularly taxis, as govt steps up efforts to reduce road crashes. From Oct 2030, all new car models would be required to be equipped with the advanced emergency braking system (AEBS), the most important ADAS feature, TOI has learnt.As for pre-2030 still-in production models, AEBS would mandatory from Oct 2032.The draft notification, with timelines for different ADAS safety features for cars, would be out soon, people aware of the development said, adding that focus would be more on taxis. They said the proposed timelines take into account the lead time that industry and users would need.ADAS is a set of more than 100 electronic technologies that increases safety by detecting potential hazards, warning the driver, and in some cases, automatically controlling brakes or steering to prevent a collision. At present, some cars have ADAS.Starting Jan 2027, new truck and bus models will have AEBS â it detects an imminent collision with a vehicle or obstacle and automatically applies brakes, if the driver fails to respond adequately, preventing a crash or reducing its severity.Blind spot information, moving off information and driver drowsiness detection and alert, and lane departure warning systems have been also made mandatory for these commercial vehicles.Itâs learnt that features, including automatic command steering functionalities, emergency lane keeping system, drowsiness and attention warning systems, would be made mandatory for taxis.The introduction of these norms could initially focus on ensuring compliance with Automotive Industry Standards for vehicles already equipped with AEBS or more advanced systems that can intervene in steering and lane-keeping, said Automobile and mobility expert Rama Pandey. âThese technologies could prove a boon for commercial drivers who spend hours behind the wheel. By shifting more safety-critical & fatigue-inducing driving decisions to automated systems, ADAS could make driving safer and less strenuous,â he added.

World.title: SC stays probe against Vijayan & kin for a week to enable him to move high court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday stayed for a week Kerala Policeâs investigation against ex-CM

and his relatives in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case and said a division bench of HC should not have refused them permission to appeal against the single judgeâs order directing an FIR and probe.

A special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, hearing appeals filed by Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and son-in-law Mohd Riyas PA, stayed the probe by state police.

Referring to Section 175(4) of BNSS, which requires a report from the public servantâs superior officer before ordering an investigation into a complaint against the public servant for acts done in discharge of official duties, the bench said, âThe single judge not only directed registration of FIR, which is the mandate in SC ruling in Vijay Madanlal case, but ordered commencement of investigation and submission of final report.

â

âCommencement of investigation and taking the same to logical conclusion will require due compliance with other statutory requirements under the special law (as laid down in Charanjit Singh judgement of Supreme Court),â it said.

âThese facts clearly make out a prima facie case of locus standi for the petitioners to seek leave to appeal against (single judgeâs) order. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned order and permit the petitioners to pursue their appeals before the division bench of the HC,â it added.





SC clarified that its observations did not touch upon the merits of the case. âThe investigation into FIR shall remain stayed for seven days,â it said.

On an ECIR registered by ED on the basis of the FIR lodged by Kerala Police, the bench said it was not expressing any opinion on its validity.

When Kerala govt undertook not to proceed with the probe till division bench decided the appeals, SC said, âYour client was so eager to investigate.

We do not appreciate the state govt functioning like this.â

On Sept 7, two years after registering an ECIR, ED shared information with state police regarding the alleged payoff case. State govt set up an SIT for a preliminary inquiry. On Oct 9, a single judge set aside the inquiry and directed filing of an FIR, lodged on Oct 12.

Vijayan told SC the alleged payments were made between 2017 and 2020 by CMRL to Exalogic, in which he was never a shareholder, director or employee. He said he had no dealings with CMRL and claimed the allegations were examined and rejected at every level up to SC, which dismissed a petition over the issue in October 2025.

World.title: PM Modi has failed ‘abysmally’ on Manipur, says Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge
World.content:
Amid fresh killings in Manipur, Congress Wednesday said BJP has only been interested in power machinations in the state and has failed to rein in violence.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi what has happened to the Peace Committee which was announced by home minister Amit Shah in June 2023 and what action has been taken on the Supreme Court-appointed Justice Gita Mittal Committeeâs recommendations.

He also asked what concrete measures have been taken to restore peace, protect citizens and address the continuing security challenges in the sensitive border state.

âBJPâs political machinations, from imposing Presidentâs Rule to replacing the CM and reinstalling its own govt, have yielded no peace.

, who did not even set foot in Manipur for nearly 29 months after violence erupted, has abysmally failed on his so-called assurance in Parliament,â the Congress president said. âAs a strategically important border state, its security and stability cannot be held hostage to the BJPâs political expediency,â Kharge added.

World.title: Tiger shooters got weapons via ‘dead drop’; couriers delivered guns a day earlier
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The shooters involved in the attack on actor Tiger Shroff received their weapons through a âdead dropâ arrangement on Oct 17, just a day before the incident. Couriers Babita and Radha â who have since been arrested â were provided the weapons at New Delhi Railway Station by the main supplier, identified as Kunal.

Kunal, who has also been arrested, has emerged as a key character who had been in touch with gangsters Anil Pandit and Randeep Malik for over two months. He had also figured as the source of the weapon used for the murder of a forex-hawala trader in Sonipat last year, sources said.

In this case, he was relaying the instructions from Pandit to the two women after dropping them at the station on Oct 15. The women reached Mumbai on Oct 17, got off at Dadar and checked into a hotel.

Around 11am, one of the shooters collected the bag with the weapons at an isolated spot near the hotel, an official added.

The dead drop method â borrowed from spycraft â has increasingly surfaced in investigations involving terror modules, drug cartels and organised crime groups of late. Agencies have unearthed non-contact logistics where handlers use encrypted messaging to direct operatives to pre-arranged locations to collect weapons, funds and synthetic drugs.

Some cases in point include IS-linked terror modules, cross-border drone-dropped payloads along the Punjab and J&K frontiers, interstate gang firearm procurements and synthetic drug delivery networks.

Investigators reconstruct digital footprints, chat logs and GPS coordinates alongside CCTV footage analysis to establish the timeline. By using technical surveillance, cell tower dumps and financial intelligence tied to encrypted communications, agencies are able to intercept these isolated drop routines to cut off unverified supplier-courier links, sources said.

World.title: At Jamnagar refinery, Rubio and Ambanis discuss energy, digital infra, giga factories
World.content:
NEW DELHI: RIL chairperson

Wednesday showcased the conglomerateâs refinery along with initiatives in data centres and new energy giga factories in Jamnagar to US secretary of state

. But oil and gas remained the centrepiece of discussions at a time when US is grappling with soaring fuel prices and low diesel stocks.

âOver the past year, Indiaâs imports of US LPG have surged from under 10% to 67%, making US Indiaâs largest LPG supplier. Relianceâs planned investment in the first new US oil refinery in 50 years is another major opportunity to expand American energy production and create jobs,â US ambassador to India Sergio Gor posted on X after the visit.

US President Donald Trump had earlier announced the setting up of a $300 billion refinery in US, with RIL being part of his plank to revive industry in the country and bring back jobs that were offshored.

The Mukesh Ambani-led company has, however, not outlined any details.

The importance of Reliance has since increased because the Jamnagar complex is where hard Venezuelan crude can be refined. The takeover of Venezuelan oil reserves by US companies has been one of Trumpâs bragging points.

Rubioâs visit to Jamnagar came amid clear signals that US is interested in enhanced processing of Venezuelan crude. Outside US, RIL is the biggest user of Venezuelan crude.





âThis is a very large and prominent energy company. They also have a pretty large investment already in US. They have extensive refining capacity. As I highlighted (earlier), this is a company, for example, that has the capability to refine the heavy crude thatâs produced in the western hemisphere, including from Venezuela, so Iâm sure thatâs a topic weâll discuss. I think through our conversations, weâll hopefully identify other opportunities to partner and work together,â Rubio said.

World.title: Jamia forms committee to draft students' union constitution amid ongoing protest
World.content:
Jamia Millia Islamia has constituted a committee to draft the constitution of its students' union, which was dissolved in 2006, amid an ongoing student protest demanding restoration of elected student representation on campus.

According to a separate notification issued by the Chief Proctor's office on Wednesday (October 21, 2026), disciplinary action initiated against protesting students between October 12 at 5:30 p.m. and October 21 will be reviewed.

The notification said students facing such action have been advised to approach the Chief Proctor. However, any cause originating after 5:30 p.m. on October 21 will invite strict disciplinary action, it added.

According to a notification issued by the Registrar's office, the committee to draft the constitution of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union (JMISU) has been constituted in furtherance of Article 23(J) and (K) of the Jamia Millia Islamia Act, 1988.

The five-member committee will be chaired by Zubair Meenai, Dean of the Faculty of Social Sciences.

The members include Luqman Ahmad Khan, Dean of the Faculty of Life Sciences, Aslam Khan of the National Medical College and Public Relations Department (NM PCR), M Amarjeet Singh of the Centre for North East Studies and Policy Research (CNESPR), and Neelofar Afzal, Dean of Students' Welfare, who will also serve as the convener.

The committee will examine the circumstances that led to the dissolution of the students' union in 2006, relevant court rulings, and the recommendations of the Lyngdoh Committee (2007).

It has been asked to consult all stakeholders, including students, and submit a draft by December 20.

The development follows the constitution of a high-level committee on October 18 to engage with protesting students and examine their demands.

According to the university administration, the panel members held discussions with student representatives on October 19 and 20, but the students did not agree to sign the minutes of the discussions.

A meeting chaired by Vice-Chancellor Mazhar Asif was held on Wednesday with members of the high-level committee, deans and other senior university officials to discuss the recommendations and explore ways to restore normalcy on campus, the university said.

The administration said it had also deployed a medical team under the supervision of the chief medical officer to monitor the health of students on hunger strike and stationed an ambulance at the protest site.

The students have been protesting at the Ghalib Lawns since October 12. The university said it had earmarked Gate No. 18 as a designated space for student protests, while appealing to students to exercise their right to dissent peacefully.

The administration also expressed concern over alleged damage to the Ghalib statue, university gates, walls and other infrastructure during the protest.

The university said it remained committed to addressing the issue of student representation in accordance with the Jamia Act, applicable ordinances and statutes, court orders and the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations.

The latest move comes amid demands for the restoration of an elected students' union at the university, where the body was dissolved nearly two decades ago.

Rejecting the notifications, student representatives said the measures failed to address their three key demands: the immediate announcement of a schedule for the 2026-27 students' union elections, revocation of disciplinary action against protesters, and removal of the Chief Proctor and the Security Advisor.

They alleged that the decision to constitute another committee to draft the union's constitution by December 20 was a delaying tactic, and objected to the Chief Proctor's notification stating that any cause arising after 5.30 pm on Wednesday would invite strict disciplinary action.

The students said their indefinite hunger strike, which began on October 12, would continue until the university released the JMISU election notification and schedule.

World.title: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong warns South Korea, says border loudspeakers to be ready within days
World.content:
North Korea will place anti-South Korea loudspeakers ​on standby along the entire border within days and ‌has put new countermeasures on alert, Kim ​Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North ⁠Korea’s leader, said on Thursday (October 22, 2026), warning Seoul of “the most horrible and distressing situation” if it continues what Pyongyang calls interference.

The ‌threats to redeploy propaganda loudspeakers, announced in Ms. Kim’s second statement within hours, risk reversing ‌South Korean President Lee Jae Myung’s signature gains ‌in ⁠easing inter-Korean tensions and pushing tensions along ⁠the heavily fortified frontier to their highest level since he took office.

In a statement carried by state media KCNA, Ms. Kim ​said she was responding to ‌a special adviser to President Lee on defence policy, who accused North Korea of planting mines that wounded South Korean soldiers and told it not ‌to escalate tensions with loudspeaker broadcasts.

“Our new counter ​means will get into the alert for duty at all the southern border line ⁠and the loudspeakers against the ROK will be on standby in a matter of days,” she said.

She ‌said North Korea would continue fortifying its southern border.

On Wednesday (October 21) evening, Ms. Kim said North Korea would activate anti-South Korea loudspeakers across the border by the end of October after visiting fortification sites with senior military officials.

South Korea says North Korean mines ‌caused a border blast last month that seriously wounded two ​soldiers. North Korea denies responsibility, calling the incident a South Korean fabrication.

Lim Eul-chul, a professor at ⁠Seoul’s Kyungnam University, said Ms. Kim’s warnings did not necessarily ⁠mean the loudspeakers would be activated.

But they present Mr. Lee’s administration with an “enormous dilemma”, he said, as ‌it faces a choice between pursuing its policy of peaceful engagement and containing aggressive North Korean ​military activity along the border.

World.title: Haryana Congress flays BJP government over its failure to keep poll promises
World.content:
Congress party on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) flayed the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), describing the functioning of the Haryana government as a complete failure and alleging a clear gap between their tall pre-poll promises and the people’s present hardships.

Senior Congress leaders in a series of press conferences across the State, criticised the government over

Deteriorating law and order, farmers’ grievances, unemployment, corruption, poor healthcare services and drug abuse are among other issues. The Congress leaders cornered the BJP on the government’s completion of two years of its third term in Haryana.

Haryana Congress In-charge Sanjay Dutt said the government has to be held accountable on issues of employment, inflation, farmers’ problems and public welfare. “What happened to the promises? Where is the development, and when will the youth, farmers, women and ordinary citizens get relief?” he said.

Mr. Dutt added that the Congress Party will not allow the people’s voice to be silenced. “We will intensify our struggle for Haryana’s rights, the protection of democracy and accountability from the BJP government. In the second year of the BJP’s third term, Haryana is in total distress. BJP must give an account of their two years to the People of Haryana,” he said.

In Sirsa, Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Rao Narender Singh said that instead of merely making claims about its achievements, the government must present a factual account of its election promises before the people.

“The BJP government had completed two years of its third term, but people across the State continued to struggle with crime, unemployment, farmers’ problems, corruption and the poor State of public services. During the Assembly elections, the BJP had made major promises to every section of society. The government must now explain how many promises have been fulfilled.”

In Chandigarh, Kumari Selja said the BJP had promised to provide women ₹2,100 every month. The government should clarify how many women were currently receiving the amount, how many were eligible in total and when the remaining eligible women would start receiving the benefit. Similarly, the government had announced free medical treatment of up to ₹10 lakh for every family. It should disclose how many families had actually received treatment coverage and how many patients had benefited.

Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda said in Rohtak that young people in Haryana deserved employment, farmers deserved fair prices for their crops, and ordinary citizens deserved a safe environment.

World.title: Delhi HC to hear on Neha Bora’s plea against ‘peace’ bond on October 22
World.content:
The Delhi High Court said it would hear on Thursday (October 22, 2026) a plea by All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora challenging a Delhi Police notice asking her to execute a “peace” bond before a Special Executive Magistrate.

Neha has sought the quashing of the notice and directions to the police not to take any coercive action in the case.

Justice Subramonium Prasad deferred the hearing at the request of Neha’s counsel.

The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), asked the AISA president to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and show cause why she should not execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 with one surety to maintain peace during the period of inquiry.

Neha was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to join the Cockroach Janata Party’s ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march. She was released on October 17.

In her petition, Neha has argued that the police notice is vague, factually incorrect and does not provide any material to substantiate the likelihood of a breach of peace.

The notice does not specify any “period, occasion or event in relation to which breach is apprehended”, the plea argued. It further contended that the proceedings amounted to a “colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of the Constitution”.

The proceedings before the SEM stem from allegations of sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and instigating people to participate in a protest at Connaught Place on the same day.

“The Impugned Notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the Petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, Connaught Place on October 16, 2026,” the petition said.

It also argued that the notice’s reference to the alleged disregard of “prohibitory orders 163 BNSS” did not identify any specific prohibitory order or incident. The only order on record, dated August 23, 2026, did not extend to Mandi House and exempted Jantar Mantar Road, it added.

World.title: Surrendered Maoist found dead in rehabilitation facility: Police
World.content:
A former Maoist — who had surrendered earlier this year — allegedly hanged himself in a government rehabilitation facility in Chhattisgarh’s Bijapur on Wednesday (October 21, 2026), said a senior police officer.

The reason behind the alleged step is not yet known.

The 26-year-old deceased Narsu Boddu took the alleged step exactly a week before he was due to complete his vocational training in agriculture as part of the government’s initiative to assist such surrendered Maoists in reintegration and achieving financial self dependence.

Before his surrender in February 2024, Boddu was a section deputy commander rank Maoist before his surrender along with other Maoists this February, said Superintendent of Police (Bijapur) Umesh Prasad Gupta.

“Around 7 a.m., fellow surrendered Maoists in the facility informed the police that Baddu was found dead in one of the bathrooms. We sent the body for post-mortem and are investigating further. Forensic teams also visited the spot,” said Mr. Gupta.

No note was found from the step. Asked if there was any history of confrontation with fellow inmates or any other history of illness, the SP replied that neither was the case. “Further probe is on,” he added.

Boddu had been lodged in the rehabilitation facility, one of the multiple such centres in different districts of the Bastar region where several waves of surrenders have happened since early 2025, since July 23 this year.

“Boddu is survived by his father, wife and two children. His mother and brother died by suicide in the past,” according to the police.

The Centre had set a deadline of March 31 this year for the elimination of Maoism from the country, following which Union Home Minister Amit Shah had declared the country free from Maoism.

World.title: 103 protected birds, turtles rescued from Moti Nagar pet shop
World.content:
About 103 birds and turtles protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act were rescued from a pet shop in Moti Nagar in the national capital on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) after animal activists informed the police about it. The rescued birds and animals include 54 parakeets, 49 turtles and the Indian Star Tortoise, said Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa.

“Legal action is under way. The animals are under veterinary care and will be released into the wild once cleared,” Mr. Sirsa said in a post on X, thanking Delhi Police and people who spoke up about it.

Animal activists Manjira Banerjee and Sahil Sharma informed the police about the illegal trade and were present when the raid happened. Mr. Sharma, a Punjab-based animal activist, said that he planned the operation after receiving hundreds of online complaints regarding alleged illegal wildlife trading in the area.

World.title: U.P. CM Yogi issues directions for strict legal action in cases of land encroachment
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) instructed officials that those who illegally occupy someone else’s land or dispossess vulnerable people must not be spared under any circumstances. Mr. Adityanath issued directions during a Janata Darshan held at Gorakhnath Temple in Gorakhpur.

“The Chief Minister instructed officials that those who illegally occupy someone else’s land or dispossess vulnerable people must not be spared under any circumstances. Strict legal action must be taken against them. If a dispute concerning land or property is familial in nature, the concerned parties should be brought together and the matter resolved through mutual dialogue,” reads an official statement.

The Chief Minister added that no one should suffer injustice. Every victim must be assisted with sensitivity. “Those who, for any reason, have been deprived of the benefits of government schemes should be provided with those benefits,” added Mr. Adityanath.

During the Janata Darshan, some people approached the Chief Minister seeking financial assistance for medical treatment. The CM assured them that the government would provide all possible assistance for their treatment. “While forwarding their applications to the officials, the Chief Minister directed that the process of preparing treatment estimates be completed as soon as possible and that the estimates be submitted to the government,” added the official statement.

During the Janata Darshan, the Chief Minister told officials, “Resolving everyone’s problems and bringing public welfare and happiness into citizens’ lives is the government’s commitment. In accordance with this commitment, the resolution of grievances must be ensured by treating every victim with sensitivity,”.

During the Janata Darshan, the Chief Minister met around 200 people. He personally approached the people seated in front of the Mahant Digvijaynath Smriti Bhawan in the temple premises and heard their problems one by one. While forwarding everyone’s applications to the concerned officials and directing them to ensure prompt and satisfactory resolution, he assured the people that the government is committed to resolving the problems of every victim.

World.title: West Bengal government sets up SIT headed by retired justice to probe Durga Puja pandal stampede
World.content:
The West Bengal government on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) issued an order setting up a special Investigation Team (SIT) to undertake a comprehensive, impartial and thorough inquiry into the stampede at Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja Pandal which claimed 19 lives on October 17.

The six-member SIT will be headed by Justice (Retired) Anindita Roy Saraswati, with several other officials of the state government and a representative of the National Disaster Response Force.

After the incident, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the SIT will be headed by a sitting judge of Calcutta High Court. However, on October 20 a Division Bench presided by Chief Justice Ravindra V. Ghuge said a sitting judge of the High Court could not be appointed to head an inquiry, in accordance with a Supreme Court directive.

The SIT shall submit its report, together with its findings and recommendations, to the State Government within three months from the date of issue of this order, the notification by the West Bengal government said.

The order signed by State’s Chief Secretary Manoj Agarwal said that the SIT will ascertain the time, location and manner in which the initial crowd surge occurred and developed into a stampede and examine the prevailing weather conditions, including relevant meteorological reports and rainfall or thunderstorm bulletins, and their possible impact on crowd movement.

The SIT will also inspect and assess the condition and adequacy of passages, barricades, stairways, gates, emergency exits and other structural and access arrangements at the pandal and examine whether permissions were granted in accordance with applicable rules and whether adequate crowd-management plans and disaster-management plans.

Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja Pandal, inaugurated by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari himself, drew large crowds this season until the tragedy occurred on the evening of October 17. Most of the deceased were women and children. Seven persons, including the organizers of the Durga Puja Pandal, have been arrested.

Questions have been raised over the role of Kolkata Police which was responsible for crowd management at the pandal. The SIT does not have a member of Kolkata police.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, for the second consecutive day, met the families of the deceased. Mr. Adhikari visited the New Barrackpore and New Town areas and handed over a cheque for ₹25 lakh to the kin of the deceased. The state government has promised compensation of ₹25 lakh to the next of kin of the deceased.

Kunal Ghosh, spokesperson of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress said that unless the BJP leaders who were in-charge of the Durga Puja pandal are arrested the SIT has no real purpose. Mr. Ghosh said that poor home guards and members of private security agency are being made a scapegoat in the stampede incident.

World.title: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia sign 'Badr' defence cooperation pact
World.content:
Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia on Wednesday signed a multilateral pact to promote cooperation in defence production and capabilities, the Turkish defence ministry said.

The signing took place in Qatar, with ministers of the four countries attending the ceremony. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif represented Pakistan at the signing.

The Foreign Office has yet to comment on the signing of the defence pact, but Asif posted on X his “key statements” on the ‘Badr Memorandum of Understanding’ (MoU).

The remarks, posted as a visual share, said: “Pakistan places great importance on strengthening defence cooperation with trusted partners. This memorandum reflects Islamabad’s shared commitment to contributing to regional peace and stability.

“We look forward to exploring opportunities for strengthening self-reliance, industrial collaboration, joint production and technology transfer while drawing on the complementary strengths of our respective defence industries, in accordance with relevant international and domestic laws and regulations.”

The statement further said, “Through this partnership, we aim to advance cooperation across joint research and development, training exchanges and industrial capability building.”

Turkiye and Qatar released similar statements on the signing of the pact.

Reuters quoted the Turkish ministry as saying that the pact, titled ‘Badr Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)’, was aimed at defence cooperation and strengthening defensive capabilities.

“The agreement holds substantial economic importance,” it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development.

“By leveraging the unique military production capabilities of each country, the initiative will facilitate cooperation and integration, enhance defence industrial capacities, and enable the fulfilment of the needs of allied and friendly nations,” it added.

Later, the Qatari defence ministry also released a similar statement.

Turkish Defence Minister Yaşar Güler, Qatar’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for Defence Sheikh Saud bin Abdulrahman, and Indonesia’s Deputy Minister of Defence Yusuf Jauhari were the other signatories. Haluk Görgün, who heads Turkiye’s Secretariat of Defence Industries, was also present on the occasion.

Görgün said in a statement that the accord formed the foundation of a “strategic cooperation” to develop joint production and technology.

“Technology sharing, joint development and strengthening domestic production capabilities lie at the heart of sustainable defence industry. As Turkiye, we value partnerships that go beyond off-the-shelf procurement models, that foster the development of a nation’s own human capital and industrial infrastructure,” Gorgun said.

“We believe that the Badr MoU will contribute to transforming the complementary capabilities of Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia, and Turkiye into concrete projects,” he added.

State-run Qatar News Agency said the pact was named ‘Badr’, “referring to the full moon, to signify how the four nations complement one another through this agreement, given its immense importance in terms of both defence and the economy”.

“Other friendly nations may join the MoU, in accordance with criteria agreed upon by the four countries,” it said.

Pakistan has strong brotherly and historic ties with the three countries, with intense diplomatic engagement seen in recent months with Qatar and Turkiye particularly.

Pakistan and Turkiye, along with Saudi Arabia, are members of the Makkah Defence Alliance, under which they are to treat an attack against any of them as an attack against all. Qatar had welcomed that pact as cooperation aimed at regional security and stability.

Islamabad and Doha have remained engaged as mediators in the US-Iran war. Meanwhile, Pakistan and Turkiye are part of the Regional Four (R4) Group along with Saudi Arabia and Egypt, which emerged in March and has met several times since then.

Earlier this week, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met his Qatari counterpart during his visit to Doha, where the two agreed to boost bilateral cooperation in internal security.

During his November 2025 visit to the Gulf state, President Asif Ali Zardari met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and offered to expand bilateral cooperation in the areas of defence production.

Last month, Indonesian naval chief Admiral Dr Muhammad Ali called on Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir in Rawalpindi.

The two sides “reaffirmed their resolve to further strengthen cooperation, particularly in the domains of professional training, defence collaboration and joint exercises”, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. The naval chief had also met President Asif Ali Zardari.

In January, Defence Minister retired Lieutenant General Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin had called on CDF Munir, with ISPR saying he expressed Jakarta’s desire to further expand defence ties with Pakistan.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.71 per litre, ups high-speed diesel rate by Re0.31
World.content:
The government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.71 per litre, but raised that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.31.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs379.31 per litre while HSD will cost Rs390.11 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 22 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Maldives president, CDF Munir stress importance of strengthening defence cooperation
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu underscored the importance of strengthening bilateral defence cooperation on Wednesday, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.

Muizzu arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday on a three-day visit at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established in 1966.

CDF Munir called on the visiting president in Islamabad, where the two leaders discussed matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment, and avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation, the Radio Pakistan report said.

“Both sides underscored the importance of strengthening defence cooperation, institutional linkages and professional exchanges,” it added.

The CDF highlighted the “longstanding and cordial relations” between the two countries. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation and promoting peace, stability and security in the region through constructive engagement, Radio Pakistan said.

It added that President Muizzu commended the professionalism of Pakistan’s armed forces and appreciated the country’s continued efforts to promote regional peace and stability.

PM Shehbaz vows strengthening of bilateral relations

Earlier, PM Shehbaz vowed to strengthen bilateral relations with the Maldives, as the two countries signed 20 memorandums of understanding (MoUs).

Addressing a joint press stakeout following the signing of 20 wide-ranging MoUs, PM Shehbaz said, “There is no doubt that the two countries [will] keep on strengthening these relations for all time to come.”

The premier extended a “very warm welcome” to the visiting dignitary and his delegation.

PM Shehbaz expressed his “warmest greetings and heartfelt affection to the people of Dhivehi Raajje, the land of islands, a nation whose spirit is as vast as the ocean that surrounds it,” hailing 60 years of diplomatic ties between the two countries.

The prime minister noted that he and Muizzu, in their bilateral and delegation-level talks, discussed “all important issues which have direct bearing between our two brotherly countries and of course, regional and international issues”.

“I am very happy to announce that we had a wonderful session, very productive and very fruitful discussions,” he remarked.

PM Shehbaz noted that the conversations encompassed “economic and trade relations, our strategic defence cooperation, our support for training of our brothers and sisters from Maldives in Pakistan in various walks of life; police, defence, education, health and many other” fields.

The prime minister went on to announce that both sides had agreed to raise their bilateral trade from $13.9 million — “just a fraction of our potential” — to $200m in the next two years.

Highlighting that the two South Asian countries had “very strong” relations, coupled with a “long list of mutual achievements”, PM Shehbaz said both sides noted that their ties “do not reflect the true strength of our economic cooperation”.

Thanking Muizzu for his “personal support in this behalf”, the premier went on to announce that Islamabad would support Malé in promoting the plantation of 5m trees in the Maldives by providing 100,000 olive cuttings and 100,000 seeds of various plant species within a mutually decided timeframe.

Referring to the MoUs signed, he affirmed that he “will be very happy to personally work with [Muizzu] to translate these written MoUs into action with prompt decision-making and speedy implementation”.

The prime minister declared that Pakistan was “absolutely ready to provide technical expertise to various segments of our mutual cooperation and, above all, Pakistan is very happy to learn that Maldives is moving forward speedily to establish data centres in other places”.

“This is great news, and as a matter of good luck, Pakistan has also attained a reasonable level of expertise and professional capability in this field,” he added, noting that the country had set up data centres in various locations. He offered Pakistan’s “experience and our professional capabilities in this behalf” to the Maldives.

PM Shehbaz noted that a large number of Maldivian students were receiving education in Pakistani universities and colleges, particularly in the field of healthcare, and that 250 Pakistani doctors and other paramedics were serving in the Maldives.

“This shall continue in future with bigger numbers so that whatever requirements you have, we as a brotherly country would be more than happy to fulfil those requirements willingly and with utmost sincerity of purpose,” the prime minister said.

Speaking on international developments, PM Shehbaz commended the Maldives’ “unwavering” support for the Palestinian cause, adding that Islamabad remains fully committed to the Palestinians’ right of self-determination and the establishment of an independent state of Palestine.

The premier further said he briefed Muizzu on Pakistan’s principled position on occupied Jammu and Kashmir, declaring Islamabad’s support for a peaceful resolution of the dispute in accordance with the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions.

“Till they have won their struggle and gotten the right of self-determination, Pakistan shall continue to support them diplomatically and, of course, support them at all international forums till they become an independent sovereign country as per UNSC resolutions, and their sacrifice will not go to waste at all,” he said.

The prime minister also expressed Pakistan’s “serious concern” over India’s decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance in April 2025, pointing out that it was a violation of an international binding treaty.

“Pakistan’s position is loud and clear and beyond an array of doubt; legally binding treaties must be respected and shared water resources must never be weaponised or used as an instrument of political pressure or blackmailing,” he stated.

PM Shehbaz said Pakistan has made it “abundantly clear at various forums”, including the UN General Assembly last month, that water was a “red line” for the country.

“Waterflows in any canal or ocean, sea or straits, carries trade, commerce, message of prosperity and progress, and not threats, confrontations and conflicts,” he said.

“Water is a lifeline for humanity […] so this should be known to all and sundry that any violation in this behalf will be regarded by Pakistan as an act of war,” the prime minister warned.

Concluding his remarks, PM Shehbaz said Muizzu’s visit had given Pakistan-Maldives relations “new purpose and new momentum”.

He remarked, “The same ocean that touches the shores of Karachi and Gwadar embraces the islands of the Maldives.

“For centuries, its waves have carried traders, scholars and travellers between our lands. Today, they carry the renewed promise of our wonderful friendship whose finest chapters are yet to be written.”

In his comments, Muizzu appreciated PM Shehbaz, the government and people of Pakistan for “their exceptional warmth and gracious hospitality”.

He added that his visit coming on the 60-year mark of Pakistan-Maldives diplomatic relations made it “particularly significant”. The 60 years have been marked by warmth, friendship and shared perspectives, he said.

“This visit takes place after a decade-long interval. It offers us an important opportunity not simply to celebrate the friendship of the past but to define the partnership of the future,” Muizzu said.

Stressing on the close relations between the two countries, he said, “Only two such longstanding friends could have talked so widely and agreed on so much about our future together”.

Muizzu said, for him, the talks represented a “clear shared ambition to move the Maldives-Pakistan partnership into a new era”.

He said the discussions encompassed several sectors including trade and investment; health and education; environment, fisheries and agriculture; youth and sports; policing and defence; training and capacity-building; and tourism.

The Maldivian president said he was pleased about the signing of 20 MoUs.

“These memoranda will open new avenues for cooperation among multiple sectors, but agreements are meaningful only when they produce results. Our next step, of course, is to translate these understandings into tangible opportunities and meaningful benefits for the people of both nations.”

Muizzu also said he endorsed the goal to take the two countries’ bilateral trade quantum from $13m to $200m in two years.

“The Maldives and Pakistan are worlds of untapped potential for each other,” the Maldivian president said.

He reaffirmed that the two countries would take a “firm step in the right direction”, adding that Thursday’s business forum would provide an opportunity to bring together business leaders, inventors and innovators from both countries to turn the friendship into mutually beneficial investments.

He said he was encouraged by the discussions to establish direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives, adding that direct flights would help support tourism as well.

He further said that the two countries’ leaders saw “considerable potential in halal and Muslim-friendly tourism”.

Moreover, Muizzu appreciated Pakistan’s scholarships and placements for Maldivian students, adding that the leaders would broaden the opportunities further, especially in artificial intelligence, digitisation and future technologies as well as health.

“We want our next generation to be prepared for the future and be prepared to shape that future.”

Muizzu stressed that climate change was “not an abstract environmental concern” for the Maldives, but “it is a direct challenge to our security, our development and our future”.

He welcomed cooperation with Pakistan in areas of climate resilience, conservation, sustainable waste management and renewable energy. He thanked PM Shehbaz for his announcement of donations to help the Maldives plant 5m trees in five years.

“Our nations share a commitment to advancing common interests through constructive engagements.”

He said the Maldives remained committed to revitalising the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, adding that “rebuilding trust, encouraging meaningful dialogue and strengthening mutual understanding are essential to unlocking the full potential of regional cooperation”.

He further expressed the Maldives’ “unequivocal and steadfast solidarity” with Palestinians and their “legitimate right to self-determination”.

Muizzu also commended Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts “to promote dialogue, de-escalation, humanitarian assistance and a just and lasting peace” in the Middle East.

Concluding his remarks, he said, “For 60 years, Pakistan has stood as a trusted friend of the Maldives.”

The two countries have now agreed to “build a new era of partnership on the foundations of our six decades of friendship”, he said.

The Maldivian president was later conferred with an honorary doctorate in politics by the International Islamic University Islamabad, with PM Shehbaz noting that the degree recognised Muizzu’s “sagacious and wise leadership and your great public service to your people in the Maldives”.

20 MoUs signed

Pakistan and the Maldives signed a series of MoUs aimed at deepening bilateral relations in multiple sectors, including defence, IT, cybersecurity, health, education, social protection, agriculture and tourism, among others.

PM Shehbaz and Muizzu were present at the ceremony where representatives from both sides exchanged the pre-signed documents.

The two countries signed an MoU on cooperation in the fields of information technology, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, digital skills, and technology and innovation. An MoU was inked to strengthen cooperation in combating illicit trafficking and abuse of narcotic drugs.

The two sides also signed an MoU on social protection as well as on health cooperation and between Maldives Food and Drug Authority and the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan.

Both nations also signed MoUs focused on the recruitment of health professionals, strengthening defence ties and maritime security cooperation.

An MoU was signed to boost agriculture cooperation, besides another one on promoting fisheries cooperation.

To promote ties in technical and vocational education, an MoU on collaboration to promote technical and vocational education and training was signed, while another MoU was inked to promote educational cooperation.

The representatives of Pakistan and the Maldives also exchanged MoUs on cooperation in the field of youth and sports development, air connectivity, tourism and in the field of arts, culture and heritage.

The MoUs were signed between the National College of Policy and Law Enforcement of the Maldives Police Service and National Police Academy, Islamabad; Civil Service Commission of Maldives and the Federal Public Service Commission of Pakistan; and Civil Service Commission of Maldives and Civil Service Academy (CSA) of Pakistan.

In order to boost commercial engagement, an MoU was signed between the Maldives State Trading Organisation (STO) and Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) for cooperation in trade of agriculture commodities, food and other products, besides signing another pact aimed at boosting cooperation in the field of environment.

Prior to the MoU signing ceremony, Muizzi was welcomed at the Prime Minister House with a guard of honour. He held introductions with federal ministers while PM Shehbaz greeted the Maldivian delegation.

According to a statement by PM Office (PMO), the prime minister extended a “warm welcome to the esteemed guest”, followed by a guard of honour by smartly turned-out contingents of all three armed forces.

The visiting dignitary also planted a sapling at PM House, and prayers were offered for the progress and prosperity of both countries.

A Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum will also be held during the visit to promote interaction between the two countries’ business communities and explore opportunities for trade and investment.

President Zardari calls for stronger bilateral economic cooperation

President Zardari also met his Maldivian counterpart at the President’s House in Islamabad, where he emphasised the need to translate the political goodwill between the two countries into “greater trade, investment, connectivity and people-to-people exchanges”.

According to a press release by the President’s Secretariat, he also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to supporting Maldives in education, healthcare, human resource development, social protection and sustainable development.

“The two leaders reviewed bilateral relations and discussed ways to strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” the statement said.

President Zardari reaffirmed the importance Pakistan attaches to its “longstanding fraternal relations” with the Maldives, highlighting that Muizzu’s state visit coincided with the 60-year anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries and provided “fresh momentum” to the bilateral partnership.

He also recalled Pakistan’s contributions to the development of the Maldives, including the Parliament building and the School of Medicine in Malé.

The press release added that both leaders expressed satisfaction over the positive trajectory of bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

They recognised the disproportionate impact of climate change on vulnerable countries, particularly small island developing states and climate-vulnerable developing economies.

“President Zardari expressed Pakistan’s readiness to deepen cooperation with Maldives in climate resilience, environmental protection and sustainable development, including support for President Muizzu’s Five Million Tree Initiative,” the statement said.

Additionally, the leaders exchanged views on regional and international developments and underscored the importance of “dialogue, diplomacy, sovereign equality, mutual respect and peaceful resolution of disputes”, it said. They also reaffirmed their support for the rights of the Palestinian people and the establishment of an independent and sovereign State of Palestine.
